data.proposedLanguage:
The Controller may audit the Processor's compliance with this Agreement and inspect the Processor's facilities, non-production systems and records used to process Personal Data, remotely where possible, but shall not access production systems or any Sub-processor's premises.
The Controller may conduct an audit once in any 12-month period on not less than 30 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours and remotely where possible. The Controller shall bear all costs of the audit unless the audit reveals a material discrepancy, in which case the Processor shall bear those costs.
The audit shall be conducted during normal business hours and shall not interfere with the Processor's operations or compromise the security of other customers' data.
The auditor shall be independent, bound by confidentiality obligations and shall not have access to the Processor's source code or to any other customer's Personal Data.
The Processor shall implement any remediation agreed following an audit within the timetable agreed in writing.
The Controller shall use reasonable endeavours to minimise disruption to the Processor's operations and to coordinate any audit of a Sub-processor through the Processor.

data.proposedLanguage:
Subject to Clause 12.2, the liability of each party under this Agreement is subject to the limitations in the MSA.
Each party shall be responsible for its own regulatory fines.
The Processor shall indemnify the Controller against any third-party claim to the extent caused by the Processor’s breach of this Agreement, subject to the limitations in the MSA.
The Controller shall indemnify the Processor against any claim arising from an instruction that is unlawful or outside the scope of the Services, provided that the Processor has notified the Controller of the issue.
Each party shall take reasonable steps to mitigate any loss arising from a breach of this Agreement.

claims.text: The clause contains or permits what the position's walk-away says we must never accept.
Judged against your published playbook position for this review.

The Processor’s indemnity is limited to third-party claims caused by its breach and is subject to the MSA limitations. The clause also allocates each party’s regulatory fines to that party, while preserving the Controller’s indemnity for unlawful or out-of-scope instructions and the mutual mitigation obligation.
Rivell suggests wording below. It is not from your playbook, so check it before you use it.

evidenceItems.text: DP-12 | DPA | Liability under the DPA is subject to the limitations in the MSA. Each party is responsible for its own regulatory fines. Bramber indemnifies the customer for third-party claims caused by Bramber's breach of the DPA, subject to the cap. The DPA continues for as long as Bramber processes personal data. | A separate data protection super-cap of 2x the annual fee, with fines allocated according to responsibility and a mutual obligation to mitigate. | An uncapped indemnity for all fines, penalties and compensation, or an obligation to indemnify the customer for the customer's own acts and omissions. | Elena Marchetti, DPO. Priya Raghavan, GC and Marcus Feld, CFO for any uncapped liability or indemnity. | A regulatory fine is the consequence of a breach of law, not a debt that can be allocated by contract. An uncapped indemnity for fines is uninsurable and would expose the company to a liability larger than its balance sheet. The MSA cap is the only defensible allocation for a business of our size.

policyFacts.escalationTrigger: Elena Marchetti, DPO. Priya Raghavan, GC and Marcus Feld, CFO for any uncapped liability or indemnity.

fallbacks: A separate data protection super-cap of 2x the annual fee, with fines allocated according to responsibility and a mutual obligation to mitigate.
policyFacts.prohibited: An uncapped indemnity for all fines, penalties and compensation, or an obligation to indemnify the customer for the customer's own acts and omissions.

The Controller generally authorizes the Processor to appoint Sub-processors.
The current Sub-processors are listed in Schedule 2. Schedule 2 shall state, for each Sub-processor, its legal name and registered address, the processing it performs and the categories of personal data concerned, and the country of processing and the transfer mechanism, where applicable. The Processor shall notify the Controller of any proposed addition or replacement at least 30 days in advance and shall provide the information necessary for the Controller to assess the change. The Controller may object to any proposed addition or replacement on reasonable data protection grounds.
The Processor shall impose data protection obligations on each Sub-processor that are no less protective than those in this Agreement, and shall remain liable to the Controller for the performance of each Sub-processor.
The Processor shall provide a copy of the relevant Sub-processor agreement to the Controller on request, subject to redaction of confidential commercial terms.

evidenceItems.text: DP-02 | DPA | Bramber processes personal data only on the customer's documented instructions, including for transfers, unless required by law. If a law requires processing, Bramber informs the customer before processing unless prohibited from doing so. The DPA and the order form together constitute the instructions. | A general instruction to provide the services in accordance with the documentation, with a change-control process for new instructions and a right to charge for instruction changes. | An obligation to comply with instructions that are unlawful, or a right for the customer to instruct processing outside the scope of the services without a change order. | Elena Marchetti, DPO. | The instruction set is what separates a processor from a controller in practice. fallbacks: A general instruction to provide the services in accordance with the documentation, with a change-control process for new instructions and a right to charge for instruction changes.

evidenceItems.text:
Processor obligations
The Processor shall comply with Article 28 of the EU GDPR and, where applicable, the UK GDPR, and shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.
The Processor shall ensure that persons authorised to process Personal Data are bound by confidentiality obligations and receive appropriate training.
The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to the Controller with data subject requests, data protection impact assessments and consultations with Supervisory Authorities, taking into account the nature of the processing and the information available to the Processor. Assistance that requires significant engineering or legal work shall be charged at the Processor's standard rates under a written scope.
The Processor shall maintain records of its processing activities in accordance with Article 30 of the EU GDPR and shall make them available to the Controller on request.
The Processor shall not engage in any processing that is inconsistent with the Controller's instructions, and shall immediately inform the Controller if an instruction infringes applicable data protection law.
The Processor shall cooperate with the Controller and with any Supervisory Authority in the investigation of a complaint or the conduct of an inspection, and shall provide information within the time reasonably requested.

evidenceItems.text: DP-11 | DPA | On termination, Bramber returns customer data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, then deletes it within 30 days, unless retention is required by law. A certificate of deletion is available on request. evidenceItems.text:
Term and termination
This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues until the later of the termination of the MSA and the completion of the deletion obligations in Clause 11.
Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect if the other party commits a material breach of this Agreement and fails to remedy it within thirty (30) days of written notice.
Termination of this Agreement does not affect the parties' obligations in respect of Personal Data processed before termination, and Clauses 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 14 survive for as long as the Processor retains Personal Data.
Subject to Clause 13.1, if the MSA terminates or expires for any reason, this Agreement terminates on the same date, without prejudice to the deletion obligations in Clause 11.

Personal data breaches
The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, of becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach.
The notification shall include, to the extent available, the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects affected, the categories and approximate volume of Personal Data affected, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed.
The Processor shall cooperate with the Controller in investigating the breach and in meeting the Controller's obligations to notify Supervisory Authorities and Data Subjects.
The Processor shall not notify any Supervisory Authority or Data Subject on the Controller's behalf without the Controller's prior written instructions, except where required by law.
The Processor shall maintain a register of all Personal Data Breaches, including those that do not require notification, and shall make the register available to the Controller on request.
The Processor shall provide a root-cause analysis and a remediation plan for each Personal Data Breach within ten (10) Business Days of the initial notification, unless the Controller agrees a longer period.

Subject to Clause 11.3, neither party shall be liable to the other for any loss of profit, loss of revenue, loss of anticipated savings, loss of business opportunity, or any indirect or consequential loss, whether in contract, tort (including negligence) or otherwise.
Subject to Clause 11.3, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by the Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
Nothing in this Clause 11 limits or excludes either party's liability for: (a) death or personal injury caused by its negligence; (b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; (c) breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality); or (d) any breach by Supplier of Clause 8 (Data Protection) or Applicable Data Protection Law.

The parties acknowledge that the limitations in this Clause 11 are a reasonable allocation of risk having regard to the Fees, the nature of the Services and the availability of insurance.
The limitations and exclusions in this Clause 11 apply notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any Order Form or SOW.
Each party shall take reasonable steps to mitigate any loss it suffers in connection with this Agreement.
The limitations in this Clause 11 apply to all claims arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether a claim is brought in contract, tort, statute or otherwise, and whether it arises before or after termination.

Definitions and interpretation
In this Agreement, the following terms have the following meanings:
Affiliate means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where “control” means the ownership of more than fifty per cent (50%) of the voting shares or the ability to direct the management of the entity.
Agreement means this Master Services Agreement, including its Schedules and any Order Form or SOW that incorporates it.
Applicable Data Protection Law means the UK GDPR, the EU GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and any other data protection or privacy law applicable to the processing of Personal Data under this Agreement.
Authorised User means an individual employee, contractor or agent of the Customer or its Affiliates who is authorised to access the Platform and for whom a user account has been created.
Business Day means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England and Wales.
Confidential Information means any information disclosed by or on behalf of a party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential from its nature and the circumstances of disclosure, but excluding information that is or becomes public without breach, is independently developed without use of the disclosed information, or is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence.
Customer Data means all data, content, documents and materials provided or made available by or on behalf of the Customer or its Authorised Users in connection with the Services, including claim files, policy records and case notes.
Deliverables means the configured workflows, reports, integrations, documentation and other materials identified as deliverables in a SOW.
Documentation means the technical and user documentation for the Platform made available by the Supplier, as updated from time to time.

nodes.text: STATEMENT OF WORK NO. 1
CLAIMS TRIAGE IMPLEMENTATION
under the Master Services Agreement dated 12 January 2026
and Order Form No. KAG-2026-014 dated 20 February 2026

This Statement of Work No. 1 is made between Kestrel Assurance Group plc, a public limited company incorporated in England and Wales with company number 04418296, whose registered office is at 1 Waterhouse Quay, Leeds LS1 4BR (the “Customer”), and Bramber Software Limited, a private limited company incorporated in England and Wales with company number 08841267, whose registered office is at The Glass Works, 12 Feeder Road, Bristol BS2 0SB (the “Supplier”).

This SOW is effective on 1 April 2026 and is governed by the Master Services Agreement dated 12 January 2026 (the “MSA”). Capitalised terms used but not defined in this SOW have the meanings given in the MSA.

Key Commercial Terms
• Customer: Kestrel Assurance Group plc
• Supplier: Bramber Software Limited
• Effective Date: 1 April 2026
• Completion Date: 30 September 2026
• Fixed Fee: £120,000
• Fees inclusive of all travel, expenses and third-party licence costs
• Liability cap: as set out in the Order Form
1. Background and objectives

1.1 The Customer's claims triage team receives approximately 48,000 new claims each year across its specialist lines. Intake is currently split between a legacy workflow tool and a set of spreadsheets maintained by team leaders.

1.2 The Customer wishes to implement Bramber Flow as its claims triage and case management platform for the delegated authority and specialty claims teams, replacing the legacy tool and the spreadsheets.
1.3 The objectives of the project are to reduce average triage time, provide a single audit trail for claim decisions, and give team leaders real-time visibility of queue performance.
1.4 The commercial terms are summarised in the key terms box above. The fee for the Services is set out in Clause 8 (Fees and expenses), and the deliverables are listed in Schedule 1.

1.5 Definitions. Capitalised terms used but not defined in this SOW have the meanings given in the MSA. In this SOW, “Deliverables” means the deliverables listed in Schedule 1, “Completion Date” means 30 September 2026, and “Supplier Background IP” has the meaning given in the MSA.
2. Scope of services

2.1 The Supplier shall design, configure, test and deploy the Platform for the Customer, migrate the in-scope claim data, integrate the Platform with the Customer's policy administration system and provide training to the Customer's claims teams.
2.2 The following work is in scope:
discovery workshops with the claims, underwriting and data teams;
configuration of the claims triage, case management and reporting modules;
migration of open claims and the last 24 months of closed claims;
integration with Meridian ClaimsCenter and Aldergate Identity;
role-based training for 450 Authorised Users and a train-the-trainer programme for 20 team leaders;
a 30-day hypercare period following go-live.
2.3 The following work is out of scope and may be provided under a separate change order:
migration of closed claims older than 24 months;
custom development of new product lines or underwriting rules;
integration with the Customer's broker portal or reinsurance systems;
data cleansing, deduplication or remediation of Customer Data.
2.4 The Supplier shall perform the Services at the Customer's premises in Leeds where reasonably required, and remotely from its Bristol office otherwise.
3. Project governance

3.1 The parties shall establish a steering committee comprising the Customer's Programme Director, the Customer's Head of Claims Operations, the Supplier's Engagement Director and the Supplier's Delivery Lead. The steering committee shall meet monthly.
3.2 Each party shall appoint a project manager. The project managers shall meet weekly, maintain the project plan and escalate risks to the steering committee.
3.3 The Supplier shall provide a written status report every Friday, including progress against the plan, risks, issues and decisions required from the Customer.

3.4 The key personnel for each party are listed in Schedule 2. Neither party shall replace a key person without the other party's prior written consent, except where the replacement is required by law or by the person's departure from the business.
4. Deliverables and milestones
4.1 The Supplier shall deliver the Deliverables in accordance with the milestones and target dates in Schedule 1.
4.2 Target dates are indicative and may be adjusted by agreement in writing where a delay is caused by the Customer's failure to provide access, data or decisions.
4.3 The Supplier shall notify the Customer at least five (5) Business Days before each milestone date if it considers that the milestone will be missed, giving reasons and a recovery plan.
5. Acceptance
5.1 The Customer shall test each Deliverable against the acceptance criteria in Schedule 1 and shall notify the Supplier of acceptance or rejection within ten (10) Business Days of delivery.
5.2 Customer may reject any Deliverable if, in its sole discretion, the Deliverable does not meet Customer's expectations.

5.3 If the Customer rejects a Deliverable, the Supplier shall remedy the non-conformity and resubmit the Deliverable within fifteen (15) Business Days. The Customer shall then have a further ten (10) Business Days to accept or reject.
5.4 Acceptance is not deemed by the passage of time. A Deliverable is accepted only when the Customer signs the acceptance certificate.
5.5 Acceptance of a Deliverable does not waive any warranty or other right of the Customer under the MSA.
6. Customer responsibilities
6.1 The Customer shall provide the Supplier with access to the claims, underwriting and data teams, the policy administration system, test environments and the data required for migration.
6.2 The Customer shall nominate a single point of contact for approvals and shall respond to requests for decisions within five (5) Business Days.
6.3 The Customer shall ensure that the Change Advisory Board reviews the release plan and provides a decision within ten (10) Business Days of submission.
6.4 The Customer is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of Customer Data provided for migration, and for obtaining any consents required for the Supplier to process it.
7. Intellectual property
7.1 The Supplier retains all right, title and interest in the Platform, the Supplier's tools, templates and know-how, and all improvements to them.
7.2 Supplier hereby assigns to Customer, with full title guarantee, all right, title and interest in and to the Deliverables, including any Supplier Background IP incorporated in them.
7.3 The Customer grants the Supplier a licence to use Customer Data solely to perform the Services and to provide support.

7.4 The Customer grants the Supplier a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use the Supplier Background IP embedded in the Deliverables solely to provide support and maintain the Platform after acceptance.
8. Fees and expenses
8.1 The fixed fee for the Deliverables is £120,000, exclusive of VAT, payable in accordance with the milestone schedule in Schedule 1.
8.2 The Supplier shall invoice the Customer on completion of each milestone. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date.
8.3 Travel and expenses incurred in accordance with the MSA will be invoiced at cost, supported by receipts, and are subject to the cap in Clause 4.5 of the MSA.

8.4 Third-party licence costs for the optional integrations listed in Schedule 1 of the Order Form are payable by the Customer at cost. Integrations marked as included are covered by the subscription Fees.
9. Data and machine learning
9.1 The parties shall comply with Schedule 4 to the MSA. The Customer is the controller and the Supplier is the processor of Personal Data processed under this SOW.
9.2 The Supplier shall process Customer Data only to perform the Services and in accordance with the Customer's documented instructions.
9.3 The Supplier may create aggregated and de-identified data from Customer Data for capacity planning and service improvement, provided that the data cannot be re-identified.
9.4 Supplier may use Customer Data, including claim notes, outcomes and any derived datasets, to train, test and improve its machine-learning models and those of its Affiliates.
9.5 The Supplier shall implement the security measures in Schedule 2 to the MSA for all environments used in the project.
10. Change control
10.1 Either party may request a change to the scope, schedule or fees by submitting a written change request to the other party's project manager.
10.2 The Supplier shall assess the impact of the change on scope, schedule, fees and resources within five (5) Business Days and provide a written change order.
10.3 No change is effective until the change order is signed by both parties. The Supplier is not obliged to perform work outside the scope until the change order is signed.
10.4 The Supplier may continue to perform the unchanged scope while a change request is under review.
11. Term and termination
11.1 This SOW begins on the Effective Date and continues until 30 September 2026, unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Clause 11.
11.2 Either party may terminate this SOW for material breach in accordance with Clause 13.3 of the MSA.

11.3 On termination, the Customer shall pay for work performed and non-cancellable commitments incurred to the date of termination, and the Supplier shall provide a written handover of work in progress.
11.4 Termination of this SOW does not terminate the MSA or any Order Form.
12. General
12.1 This SOW incorporates the MSA. In the event of a conflict, the order of precedence in Clause 2.3 of the MSA applies.
12.2 This SOW, together with the MSA and the Order Form, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties in relation to the project.
12.3 Notices under this SOW shall be given in accordance with Clause 17 of the MSA, with a copy to the Customer's Programme Director and the Supplier's Engagement Director.
12.4 This SOW is governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

This Master Services Agreement is made on 12 January 2026 between:

(1) KESTREL ASSURANCE GROUP PLC, a public limited company incorporated in England and Wales with company number 04418296, whose registered office is at 1 Waterhouse Quay, Leeds LS1 4BR (the “Customer”); and

(2) BRAMBER SOFTWARE LIMITED, a private limited company incorporated in England and Wales with company number 08841267, whose registered office is at The Glass Works, 12 Feeder Road, Bristol BS2 0SB (the “Supplier”).
The Customer and the Supplier are each a “party” and together the “parties”.
Recitals

(A) The Customer is a specialty insurance group that underwrites commercial and specialist personal lines through brokers and managing general agents in the United Kingdom, Ireland and the United States.
(B) The Supplier provides a cloud-based workflow and case management platform known as Bramber Flow, together with implementation, configuration and support services.
(C) The Customer wishes to procure the Services for its claims triage and delegated authority teams, and the Supplier is willing to provide them on the terms of this Agreement.
(D) This Agreement supersedes the evaluation agreement between the parties dated 3 November 2025, which terminates on the Effective Date without further liability.
The parties agree as follows:
Definitions and interpretation
In this Agreement, the following terms have the following meanings:

Affiliate means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where “control” means the ownership of more than fifty per cent (50%) of the voting shares or the ability to direct the management of the entity.
Agreement means this Master Services Agreement, including its Schedules and any Order Form or SOW that incorporates it.

Applicable Data Protection Law means the UK GDPR, the EU GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and any other data protection or privacy law applicable to the processing of Personal Data under this Agreement.
Authorised User means an individual employee, contractor or agent of the Customer or its Affiliates who is authorised to access the Platform and for whom a user account has been created.
Business Day means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England and Wales.

Confidential Information means any information disclosed by or on behalf of a party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential from its nature and the circumstances of disclosure, but excluding information that is or becomes public without breach, is independently developed without use of the disclosed information, or is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence.

Customer Data means all data, content, documents and materials provided or made available by or on behalf of the Customer or its Authorised Users in connection with the Services, including claim files, policy records and case notes.
Deliverables means the configured workflows, reports, integrations, documentation and other materials identified as deliverables in a SOW.
Documentation means the technical and user documentation for the Platform made available by the Supplier, as updated from time to time.
Effective Date means 1 April 2026.
Fees means the subscription, implementation, support and other charges set out in an Order Form or SOW, exclusive of VAT.

Force Majeure Event means an event or circumstance beyond a party's reasonable control, including natural disaster, war, terrorism, civil disorder, epidemic, failure of public infrastructure, and a failure of a third-party provider that could not have been avoided by reasonable planning, but excluding any failure of a subcontractor or other provider engaged by the Supplier.

Intellectual Property Rights means patents, trade marks, service marks, trade names, copyright, database rights, design rights, domain names, rights in software, rights in confidential information and all other intellectual property rights, whether registered or unregistered, together with all applications and renewals.
Order Form means an order form signed by both parties that identifies the Services, the Subscription Term, the Fees and any additional terms, and that incorporates this Agreement.
Personal Data means personal data as defined in Applicable Data Protection Law that is processed by the Supplier on behalf of the Customer under this Agreement.
Platform means the Bramber Flow cloud workflow and case management platform, including the software, application programming interfaces and infrastructure operated by or on behalf of the Supplier.
Professional Services means the implementation, configuration, integration, training and advisory services described in a SOW.
Services means the subscription to the Platform, the Support, the Professional Services and any other services described in an Order Form or SOW.
SOW means a statement of work signed by both parties that describes a project, its deliverables, milestones, acceptance criteria and fees, and that incorporates this Agreement.
Subscription Term means the period during which the Customer is entitled to access and use the Platform, as set out in an Order Form.
Support means the support and maintenance services described in Schedule 1.

Supplier Background IP means the Platform, the Documentation, the Supplier's tools, templates, methodologies and know-how, and all Intellectual Property Rights in them, excluding Customer Data and the bespoke Deliverables.
Third-Party Services means software, data, connectivity or other services supplied by a third party that are identified in an Order Form or SOW and used in connection with the Services.
VAT means value added tax or any equivalent sales tax.
In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation;
(b) the singular includes the plural and vice versa, and a reference to a person includes a body corporate and an unincorporated body;
(c) “including” means “including without limitation”;
(d) a reference to a statute includes any amendment, re-enactment or subordinate legislation made under it; and
(e) a reference to a clause or Schedule is to a clause of, or Schedule to, this Agreement.
Ordering and structure

Subject to the terms of this Agreement, the Supplier grants the Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable right to access and use the Platform and to receive the Support during the Subscription Term, solely for the Customer's internal business purposes and in accordance with the Documentation.
The Customer may order Services by signing an Order Form. Each Order Form incorporates this Agreement and is governed by it. An Order Form may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature.
In the event of a conflict between the documents forming this Agreement, the following order of precedence applies: (a) the Order Form; (b) the SOW; (c) this Agreement; and (d) the Documentation.
The Customer's Affiliates may purchase Services under this Agreement by signing an Order Form, provided that the Customer remains responsible for each Affiliate's compliance with this Agreement.
The Supplier may update the Documentation from time to time, provided that no update materially reduces the functionality of the Services during a Subscription Term.
Implementation and acceptance
The Supplier shall provide the Professional Services in accordance with the applicable SOW and with reasonable skill and care.

Where a SOW identifies Deliverables and acceptance criteria, the Customer shall test each Deliverable against those criteria and shall notify the Supplier in writing of any material non-conformity within ten (10) Business Days of delivery. If the Customer does not give a notice within that period, the Deliverable is deemed accepted.

A rejection notice must identify the specific acceptance criterion that has not been met and provide reasonable evidence of the failure. The Supplier shall correct the non-conformity within twenty (20) Business Days and resubmit the Deliverable for acceptance testing.
The Customer may not reject a Deliverable for a defect that is immaterial, that arises from Customer Data or Third-Party Services, or that results from a configuration requested by the Customer.
Acceptance of a Deliverable does not relieve the Supplier of its obligations under Clause 9 or its obligation to provide the Services in accordance with this Agreement.
Fees, invoicing and payment
The Customer shall pay the Fees set out in the applicable Order Form or SOW. Fees are exclusive of VAT, which shall be added at the prevailing rate.

The Supplier shall invoice subscription Fees monthly in arrears and Professional Services Fees in accordance with the milestone schedule in the SOW. Invoices are payable within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date.

The Customer shall notify the Supplier in writing of any disputed invoice within ten (10) Business Days of the invoice date, giving reasons for the dispute. The Customer shall pay all undisputed amounts when due and shall not withhold payment of the whole invoice.

Late payment shall attract interest at four per cent (4%) above the Bank of England base rate from the due date until payment, calculated daily. The Supplier may suspend the Services on thirty (30) days' written notice if undisputed Fees remain unpaid for more than sixty (60) days.

The Customer shall reimburse pre-approved travel and expenses incurred by the Supplier in providing Professional Services at cost, supported by receipts. Expenses shall not exceed five per cent (5%) of the Professional Services Fees unless approved in writing in advance.
The Customer may not set off any amount against Fees unless the amount has been agreed in writing by the Supplier or awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction.

Each party shall be responsible for its own taxes on its own income. If any deduction or withholding is required by law, the Customer shall increase the payment so that the Supplier receives the amount it would have received without the deduction.
Customer obligations

The Customer shall provide the Supplier with timely access to its personnel, systems, data and facilities reasonably required to provide the Services, and shall ensure that its Authorised Users comply with this Agreement and the Documentation.

The Customer is responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of its Authorised Users' credentials and for all activity that occurs under its accounts, except to the extent caused by the Supplier's breach of this Agreement.

The Customer shall not use the Services in any manner that is unlawful, fraudulent or harmful to Supplier's reputation or commercial interests, and shall comply with the acceptable use policy set out in the Documentation.

The Customer is responsible for the accuracy, quality and lawfulness of Customer Data and for obtaining all consents and permissions required for the Supplier to process it in accordance with this Agreement.

The Customer shall notify the Supplier promptly, and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours, if it becomes aware of any unauthorised access to the Platform or any security incident affecting Customer Data.
The Customer shall not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble any part of the Platform, or use the Services to build a competing product, except to the extent permitted by law.
Intellectual property

The Supplier owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Platform, the Documentation, the Supplier's tools, templates, methodologies and know-how, and all Intellectual Property Rights in them, including any improvements, modifications or derivative works made during the Subscription Term.
The Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights in it.

Subject to payment of the applicable Fees, the Supplier assigns to the Customer all right, title and interest in and to the bespoke Deliverables identified in a SOW, excluding the Supplier Background IP. The Supplier grants the Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use the Supplier Background IP embedded in the Deliverables solely as necessary to use them for the Customer's internal business purposes.
The Customer grants the Supplier a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to process Customer Data solely to provide the Services and to comply with Applicable Law.

The Customer grants the Supplier a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use any feedback, suggestions or ideas it provides about the Services, provided that the Supplier does not identify the Customer as the source without consent.
Each party reserves all rights not expressly granted to the other under this Agreement.
Confidentiality

Each party shall keep the other's Confidential Information confidential, use it only for the purposes of this Agreement, and disclose it only to its personnel, Affiliates and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Clause.

The receiving party shall protect the disclosing party's Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care that it uses for its own confidential information, and in any event no less than reasonable care.
The obligations in this Clause survive for five (5) years after termination or expiry of this Agreement, except for trade secrets, which are protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.

Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes public without breach of this Agreement, is independently developed by the receiving party without use of the disclosed information, or is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence.

The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information where required by law, a regulator or a court of competent jurisdiction, provided that it gives the disclosing party prompt written notice where lawful and discloses only the minimum information required.

On termination or on written request, the receiving party shall return or destroy the disclosing party's Confidential Information and certify destruction on request, except for one copy retained for legal or regulatory compliance.
Each party acknowledges that damages may be an inadequate remedy for breach of this Clause and that the disclosing party may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy.

Nothing in this Clause restricts either party from using general knowledge, skills and experience retained in unaided memory, provided that it does not use any document, dataset, model or intentionally memorised information.
Data protection
The parties shall comply with Schedule 4 (Data Processing). The Customer is the controller and the Supplier is the processor of Personal Data.

The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the Customer's documented instructions, which comprise this Agreement, the applicable Order Form, the SOW and the Customer's configuration of the Platform, unless required by law.
The Supplier shall implement and maintain the technical and organisational measures set out in Schedule 2 and Schedule 4.
The Supplier may appoint sub-processors in accordance with Schedule 4 and shall remain liable for their performance.

The Supplier shall provide reasonable assistance to the Customer with data subject requests, data protection impact assessments and consultations with supervisory authorities, taking into account the nature of the processing.
The Supplier shall not transfer Personal Data outside the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area except in accordance with Schedule 4 and Applicable Data Protection Law.
The Supplier shall notify the Customer without undue delay, and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours, of becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Personal Data.
On termination, the Supplier shall return Personal Data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and delete it in accordance with Schedule 4, unless retention is required by law.
The Supplier shall make available all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Clause and shall allow for audits in accordance with Clause 14.
Warranties
The Supplier warrants that the Platform will perform materially in accordance with the Documentation during the Subscription Term.

If the Platform does not comply with Clause 9.1, the Customer shall notify the Supplier in writing within thirty (30) days of becoming aware of the non-conformity. The Supplier shall use reasonable endeavours to correct the non-conformity within thirty (30) days, or provide a reasonable workaround.
The Supplier warrants that the Professional Services will be performed with reasonable skill and care by suitably qualified personnel.
The Supplier warrants that it will not knowingly introduce malware into the Platform and that it maintains commercially reasonable measures to prevent unauthorised access.
The Customer warrants that it has the right to provide Customer Data to the Supplier and that its instructions comply with Applicable Law.

Except as expressly set out in this Agreement, all warranties, conditions and terms, whether express or implied by statute, common law or otherwise, are excluded to the fullest extent permitted by law. Nothing in this Clause excludes any warranty that cannot be excluded by law.
Indemnities

The Supplier shall indemnify the Customer against any third-party claim that the Platform, when used in accordance with this Agreement, infringes that third party's Intellectual Property Rights, subject to Clause 11.

The indemnity in Clause 10.1 does not apply to the extent that the claim arises from Customer Data, Third-Party Services, a modification of the Platform not made by the Supplier, or use of the Platform in combination with anything not supplied or approved by the Supplier.

The Customer shall indemnify the Supplier against any third-party claim arising from Customer Data, the Customer's breach of Applicable Law, or the Customer's use of the Services outside the scope of this Agreement.

The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party sole control of the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.
The indemnifying party shall not settle a claim in a way that admits fault by, or imposes a non-monetary obligation on, the indemnified party without its written consent.
Limitation of liability

Subject to Clause 11.3, neither party shall be liable to the other for any loss of profit, loss of revenue, loss of anticipated savings, loss of business opportunity, or any indirect or consequential loss, whether in contract, tort (including negligence) or otherwise.

Subject to Clause 11.3, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by the Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

Nothing in this Clause 11 limits or excludes either party's liability for: (a) death or personal injury caused by its negligence; (b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; (c) breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality); or (d) any breach by Supplier of Clause 8 (Data Protection) or Applicable Data Protection Law.
The cap in Clause 11.2 does not apply to the Customer's obligation to pay Fees properly due, or to either party's liability for breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality).
The parties acknowledge that the limitations in this Clause 11 are a reasonable allocation of risk having regard to the Fees, the nature of the Services and the availability of insurance.
The limitations and exclusions in this Clause 11 apply notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any Order Form or SOW.
Each party shall take reasonable steps to mitigate any loss it suffers in connection with this Agreement.

The limitations in this Clause 11 apply to all claims arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether a claim is brought in contract, tort, statute or otherwise, and whether it arises before or after termination.
Insurance

The Supplier shall maintain, with a reputable insurer, professional indemnity insurance of at least £10,000,000, cyber liability insurance of at least £10,000,000, public liability insurance of at least £5,000,000 and employer's liability insurance of at least £5,000,000.
The Supplier shall provide certificates of insurance to the Customer on request, and shall notify the Customer if any policy is cancelled or materially reduced.
The Supplier's insurance shall respond to claims covered by it in accordance with its terms, but the existence of insurance does not increase or otherwise affect the limitations in Clause 11.
Term and termination
This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three (3) years, unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Clause 13.

At the end of the initial term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of twelve (12) months unless either party gives written notice at least one hundred and twenty (120) days before the end of the then-current term.
Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other party commits a material breach and fails to remedy it within thirty (30) days of written notice.

Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, enters administration, has a receiver appointed, or ceases to carry on business.
The Supplier may suspend the Services if the Customer fails to pay undisputed Fees in accordance with Clause 4, or if suspension is necessary to prevent a security incident or unlawful use.

Termination of this Agreement does not affect any accrued rights or liabilities of either party, and the provisions that by their nature should survive termination shall survive, including Clauses 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 14, 17, 18 and 19.

On termination, the Customer shall pay all Fees accrued to the effective date of termination. The Supplier shall provide the exit assistance described in Schedule 1 for ninety (90) days at its standard rates.
Audit and records

The Supplier shall maintain complete and accurate records of its provision of the Services and its compliance with this Agreement for a period of six (6) years after the end of the year to which the records relate.

The Customer may, on at least five (5) Business Days' prior written notice and no more than twice in any twelve-month period, audit Supplier's compliance with this Agreement, including access to Supplier's personnel, systems and sub-processors.

The audit shall be conducted during normal business hours, remotely where possible, and shall not interfere with the Supplier's operations or compromise the security or confidentiality of other customers' data.
The auditor shall be independent, bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as Clause 7, and shall not have access to the Supplier's source code or to any other customer's data.
The Customer shall bear the cost of the audit unless the audit reveals a material discrepancy of more than five per cent (5%) in the Fees or a material breach of Schedule 2.
Subcontracting

The Supplier may subcontract any part of the Services to its Affiliates or to third parties, provided that it remains responsible for the performance of the subcontracted Services and imposes obligations on the subcontractor that are consistent with this Agreement.
The Supplier shall list its sub-processors in Schedule 4 and shall notify the Customer of any change in accordance with that Schedule.
The Supplier shall not subcontract the provision of the Platform to a direct competitor of the Customer without the Customer's prior written consent.
Any subcontracting does not relieve the Supplier of its obligations under this Agreement.
Force majeure

A party is not liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Agreement to the extent caused by a Force Majeure Event, provided that it notifies the other party promptly and uses reasonable endeavours to mitigate the effect.
A Force Majeure Event does not excuse the Customer from paying Fees for Services already provided.

If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than sixty (60) days, either party may terminate the affected Order Form or SOW on written notice without liability, except for Fees accrued to the date of termination.
Notices
Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand or by recorded post to the addresses set out below, with a copy to the recipient's legal department.
Notices to the Customer shall be sent to Kestrel Assurance Group plc, 1 Waterhouse Quay, Leeds LS1 4BR, for the attention of the General Counsel, with a copy to the Head of Procurement.
Notices to the Supplier shall be sent to Bramber Software Limited, The Glass Works, 12 Feeder Road, Bristol BS2 0SB, for the attention of the General Counsel.
A notice is deemed received on delivery, if delivered by hand, or two Business Days after posting, if sent by recorded post.
Governing law and disputes
This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by the laws of England and Wales.
The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales sitting in Leeds.

Before commencing proceedings, the parties shall escalate the dispute to their respective senior representatives, who shall meet within ten (10) Business Days and attempt in good faith to resolve it for a further twenty (20) Business Days.
Nothing in this Clause prevents either party from applying for injunctive relief or other urgent relief at any time.
General

This Agreement, together with the Order Forms, SOWs and Schedules, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior discussions, proposals and representations, except for fraudulent misrepresentation.
No variation of this Agreement is effective unless made in writing and signed by authorised representatives of both parties.

Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all of its assets, provided that the assignee assumes the assigning party's obligations in writing.
No failure or delay in exercising a right operates as a waiver of that right, and no single exercise prevents any further exercise.

If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect, and the parties shall negotiate a valid replacement that achieves the original commercial intent.
A person who is not a party to this Agreement has no right under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 to enforce any provision of it.

Neither party shall use the other's name, logo or trademarks in any press release, advertisement, case study or public communication without the other's prior written consent, except that the Supplier may include the Customer's name in a confidential list of reference customers provided to prospective customers under a written confidentiality obligation.
Each party shall comply with all applicable anti-bribery, anti-money laundering and sanctions laws, and shall not offer or accept any bribe or improper payment in connection with this Agreement.
The parties shall comply with all applicable export control and sanctions laws in relation to the Services and Customer Data.
This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.
The headings in this Agreement are for convenience only and do not affect its interpretation.

(A) The Customer is a specialty insurance group that underwrites commercial and specialist personal lines through brokers and managing general agents in the United Kingdom, Ireland and the United States.
(B) The Supplier provides a cloud-based workflow and case management platform known as Bramber Flow, together with implementation, configuration and support services.
(C) The Customer wishes to procure the Services for its claims triage and delegated authority teams, and the Supplier is willing to provide them on the terms of this Agreement.
(D) This Agreement supersedes the evaluation agreement between the parties dated 3 November 2025, which terminates on the Effective Date without further liability.
The parties agree as follows:

clauses.heading: Definitions and interpretation
clauses.contentText:
Definitions and interpretation
In this Agreement, the following terms have the following meanings:
Affiliate means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where “control” means the ownership of more than fifty per cent (50%) of the voting shares or the ability to direct the management of the entity.
Agreement means this Master Services Agreement, including its Schedules and any Order Form or SOW that incorporates it.
Applicable Data Protection Law means the UK GDPR, the EU GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and any other data protection or privacy law applicable to the processing of Personal Data under this Agreement.
Authorised User means an individual employee, contractor or agent of the Customer or its Affiliates who is authorised to access the Platform and for whom a user account has been created.
Business Day means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England and Wales.
Confidential Information means any information disclosed by or on behalf of a party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential from its nature and the circumstances of disclosure, but excluding information that is or becomes public without breach, is independently developed without use of the disclosed information, or is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence.
Customer Data means all data, content, documents and materials provided or made available by or on behalf of the Customer or its Authorised Users in connection with the Services, including claim files, policy records and case notes.
Deliverables means the configured workflows, reports, integrations, documentation and other materials identified as deliverables in a SOW.
Documentation means the technical and user documentation for the Platform made available by the Supplier, as updated from time to time.
Effective Date means 1 April 2026.
Fees means the subscription, implementation, support and other charges set out in an Order Form or SOW, exclusive of VAT.
Force Majeure Event means an event or circumstance beyond a party's reasonable control, including natural disaster, war, terrorism, civil disorder, epidemic, failure of public infrastructure, and a failure of a third-party provider that could not have been avoided by reasonable planning, but excluding any failure of a subcontractor or other provider engaged by the Supplier.
Intellectual Property Rights means patents, trade marks, service marks, trade names, copyright, database rights, design rights, domain names, rights in software, rights in confidential information and all other intellectual property rights, whether registered or unregistered, together with all applications and renewals.
Order Form means an order form signed by both parties that identifies the Services, the Subscription Term, the Fees and any additional terms, and that incorporates this Agreement.
Personal Data means personal data as defined in Applicable Data Protection Law that is processed by the Supplier on behalf of the Customer under this Agreement.
Platform means the Bramber Flow cloud workflow and case management platform, including the software, application programming interfaces and infrastructure operated by or on behalf of the Supplier.
Professional Services means the implementation, configuration, integration, training and advisory services described in a SOW.
Services means the subscription to the Platform, the Support, the Professional Services and any other services described in an Order Form or SOW.
SOW means a statement of work signed by both parties that describes a project, its deliverables, milestones, acceptance criteria and fees, and that incorporates this Agreement.
Subscription Term means the period during which the Customer is entitled to access and use the Platform, as set out in an Order Form.
Support means the support and maintenance services described in Schedule 1.
Supplier Background IP means the Platform, the Documentation, the Supplier's tools, templates, methodologies and know-how, and all Intellectual Property Rights in them, excluding Customer Data and the bespoke Deliverables.
Third-Party Services means software, data, connectivity or other services supplied by a third party that are identified in an Order Form or SOW and used in connection with the Services.
VAT means value added tax or any equivalent sales tax.
In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires:
(a) headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation;
(b) the singular includes the plural and vice versa, and a reference to a person includes a body corporate and an unincorporated body;
(c) “including” means “including without limitation”;
(d) a reference to a statute includes any amendment, re-enactment or subordinate legislation made under it; and
(e) a reference to a clause or Schedule is to a clause of, or Schedule to, this Agreement.

clauses.heading: Ordering and structure
clauses.contentText:
Ordering and structure
Subject to the terms of this Agreement, the Supplier grants the Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable right to access and use the Platform and to receive the Support during the Subscription Term, solely for the Customer's internal business purposes and in accordance with the Documentation.
The Customer may order Services by signing an Order Form. Each Order Form incorporates this Agreement and is governed by it. An Order Form may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature.
In the event of a conflict between the documents forming this Agreement, the following order of precedence applies: (a) the Order Form; (b) the SOW; (c) this Agreement; and (d) the Documentation.
The Customer's Affiliates may purchase Services under this Agreement by signing an Order Form, provided that the Customer remains responsible for each Affiliate's compliance with this Agreement.
The Supplier may update the Documentation from time to time, provided that no update materially reduces the functionality of the Services during a Subscription Term.

clauses.heading: Implementation and acceptance
clauses.contentText:
Implementation and acceptance
The Supplier shall provide the Professional Services in accordance with the applicable SOW and with reasonable skill and care.
Where a SOW identifies Deliverables and acceptance criteria, the Customer shall test each Deliverable against those criteria and shall notify the Supplier in writing of any material non-conformity within ten (10) Business Days of delivery. If the Customer does not give a notice within that period, the Deliverable is deemed accepted.
A rejection notice must identify the specific acceptance criterion that has not been met and provide reasonable evidence of the failure. The Supplier shall correct the non-conformity within twenty (20) Business Days and resubmit the Deliverable for acceptance testing.
The Customer may not reject a Deliverable for a defect that is immaterial, that arises from Customer Data or Third-Party Services, or that results from a configuration requested by the Customer.
Acceptance of a Deliverable does not relieve the Supplier of its obligations under Clause 9 or its obligation to provide the Services in accordance with this Agreement.

clauses.heading: Fees, invoicing and payment
clauses.contentText:
Fees, invoicing and payment
The Customer shall pay the Fees set out in the applicable Order Form or SOW. Fees are exclusive of VAT, which shall be added at the prevailing rate.
The Supplier shall invoice subscription Fees monthly in arrears and Professional Services Fees in accordance with the milestone schedule in the SOW. Invoices are payable within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date.
The Customer shall notify the Supplier in writing of any disputed invoice within ten (10) Business Days of the invoice date, giving reasons for the dispute. The Customer shall pay all undisputed amounts when due and shall not withhold payment of the whole invoice.
Late payment shall attract interest at four per cent (4%) above the Bank of England base rate from the due date until payment, calculated daily. The Supplier may suspend the Services on thirty (30) days' written notice if undisputed Fees remain unpaid for more than sixty (60) days.
The Customer shall reimburse pre-approved travel and expenses incurred by the Supplier in providing Professional Services at cost, supported by receipts. Expenses shall not exceed five per cent (5%) of the Professional Services Fees unless approved in writing in advance.
The Customer may not set off any amount against Fees unless the amount has been agreed in writing by the Supplier or awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction.
Each party shall be responsible for its own taxes on its own income. If any deduction or withholding is required by law, the Customer shall increase the payment so that the Supplier receives the amount it would have received without the deduction.

clauses.heading: Customer obligations
clauses.contentText:
Customer obligations
The Customer shall provide the Supplier with timely access to its personnel, systems, data and facilities reasonably required to provide the Services, and shall ensure that its Authorised Users comply with this Agreement and the Documentation.
The Customer is responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of its Authorised Users' credentials and for all activity that occurs under its accounts, except to the extent caused by the Supplier's breach of this Agreement.
The Customer shall not use the Services in any manner that is unlawful, fraudulent or harmful to Supplier's reputation or commercial interests, and shall comply with the acceptable use policy set out in the Documentation.
The Customer is responsible for the accuracy, quality and lawfulness of Customer Data and for obtaining all consents and permissions required for the Supplier to process it in accordance with this Agreement.
The Customer shall notify the Supplier promptly, and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours, if it becomes aware of any unauthorised access to the Platform or any security incident affecting Customer Data.
The Customer shall not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble any part of the Platform, or use the Services to build a competing product, except to the extent permitted by law.

clauses.heading: Intellectual property
clauses.contentText:
Intellectual property
The Supplier owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Platform, the Documentation, the Supplier's tools, templates, methodologies and know-how, and all Intellectual Property Rights in them, including any improvements, modifications or derivative works made during the Subscription Term.
The Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights in it.
Subject to payment of the applicable Fees, the Supplier assigns to the Customer all right, title and interest in and to the bespoke Deliverables identified in a SOW, excluding the Supplier Background IP. The Supplier grants the Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use the Supplier Background IP embedded in the Deliverables solely as necessary to use them for the Customer's internal business purposes.
The Customer grants the Supplier a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to process Customer Data solely to provide the Services and to comply with Applicable Law.
The Customer grants the Supplier a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use any feedback, suggestions or ideas it provides about the Services, provided that the Supplier does not identify the Customer as the source without consent.
Each party reserves all rights not expressly granted to the other under this Agreement.

clauses.heading: Confidentiality
clauses.contentText:
Confidentiality
Each party shall keep the other's Confidential Information confidential, use it only for the purposes of this Agreement, and disclose it only to its personnel, Affiliates and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Clause.
The receiving party shall protect the disclosing party's Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care that it uses for its own confidential information, and in any event no less than reasonable care.
The obligations in this Clause survive for five (5) years after termination or expiry of this Agreement, except for trade secrets, which are protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.
Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes public without breach of this Agreement, is independently developed by the receiving party without use of the disclosed information, or is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence.
The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information where required by law, a regulator or a court of competent jurisdiction, provided that it gives the disclosing party prompt written notice where lawful and discloses only the minimum information required.
On termination or on written request, the receiving party shall return or destroy the disclosing party's Confidential Information and certify destruction on request, except for one copy retained for legal or regulatory compliance.
Each party acknowledges that damages may be an inadequate remedy for breach of this Clause and that the disclosing party may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy.
Nothing in this Clause restricts either party from using general knowledge, skills and experience retained in unaided memory, provided that it does not use any document, dataset, model or intentionally memorised information.

clauses.heading: Data protection
clauses.contentText:
Data protection
The parties shall comply with Schedule 4 (Data Processing). The Customer is the controller and the Supplier is the processor of Personal Data.
The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the Customer's documented instructions, which comprise this Agreement, the applicable Order Form, the SOW and the Customer's configuration of the Platform, unless required by law.
The Supplier shall implement and maintain the technical and organisational measures set out in Schedule 2 and Schedule 4.
The Supplier may appoint sub-processors in accordance with Schedule 4 and shall remain liable for their performance.
The Supplier shall provide reasonable assistance to the Customer with data subject requests, data protection impact assessments and consultations with supervisory authorities, taking into account the nature of the processing.
The Supplier shall not transfer Personal Data outside the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area except in accordance with Schedule 4 and Applicable Data Protection Law.
The Supplier shall notify the Customer without undue delay, and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours, of becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Personal Data.
On termination, the Supplier shall return Personal Data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and delete it in accordance with Schedule 4, unless retention is required by law.
The Supplier shall make available all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Clause and shall allow for audits in accordance with Clause 14.

clauses.heading: Warranties
clauses.contentText:
Warranties
The Supplier warrants that the Platform will perform materially in accordance with the Documentation during the Subscription Term.
If the Platform does not comply with Clause 9.1, the Customer shall notify the Supplier in writing within thirty (30) days of becoming aware of the non-conformity. The Supplier shall use reasonable endeavours to correct the non-conformity within thirty (30) days, or provide a reasonable workaround.
The Supplier warrants that the Professional Services will be performed with reasonable skill and care by suitably qualified personnel.
The Supplier warrants that it will not knowingly introduce malware into the Platform and that it maintains commercially reasonable measures to prevent unauthorised access.
The Customer warrants that it has the right to provide Customer Data to the Supplier and that its instructions comply with Applicable Law.
Except as expressly set out in this Agreement, all warranties, conditions and terms, whether express or implied by statute, common law or otherwise, are excluded to the fullest extent permitted by law. Nothing in this Clause excludes any warranty that cannot be excluded by law.

clauses.heading: Indemnities
clauses.contentText:
Indemnities
The Supplier shall indemnify the Customer against any third-party claim that the Platform, when used in accordance with this Agreement, infringes that third party's Intellectual Property Rights, subject to Clause 11.
The indemnity in Clause 10.1 does not apply to the extent that the claim arises from Customer Data, Third-Party Services, a modification of the Platform not made by the Supplier, or use of the Platform in combination with anything not supplied or approved by the Supplier.
The Customer shall indemnify the Supplier against any third-party claim arising from Customer Data, the Customer's breach of Applicable Law, or the Customer's use of the Services outside the scope of this Agreement.
The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party sole control of the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.
The indemnifying party shall not settle a claim in a way that admits fault by, or imposes a non-monetary obligation on, the indemnified party without its written consent.

clauses.heading: Limitation of liability
clauses.contentText:
Limitation of liability
Subject to Clause 11.3, neither party shall be liable to the other for any loss of profit, loss of revenue, loss of anticipated savings, loss of business opportunity, or any indirect or consequential loss, whether in contract, tort (including negligence) or otherwise.
Subject to Clause 11.3, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by the Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
Nothing in this Clause 11 limits or excludes either party's liability for: (a) death or personal injury caused by its negligence; (b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; (c) breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality); or (d) any breach by Supplier of Clause 8 (Data Protection) or Applicable Data Protection Law.
The cap in Clause 11.2 does not apply to the Customer's obligation to pay Fees properly due, or to either party's liability for breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality).
The parties acknowledge that the limitations in this Clause 11 are a reasonable allocation of risk having regard to the Fees, the nature of the Services and the availability of insurance.
The limitations and exclusions in this Clause 11 apply notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any Order Form or SOW.
Each party shall take reasonable steps to mitigate any loss it suffers in connection with this Agreement.
The limitations in this Clause 11 apply to all claims arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether a claim is brought in contract, tort, statute or otherwise, and whether it arises before or after termination.
