data.text: Approved clauses, variants and guidance for customer contracts
MSAs, order forms, statements of work, DPAs and NDAs

This library contains the clauses we use most often in customer MSAs, order forms and statements of work. Each clause has a preferred version and, where we have agreed one, up to two fallbacks. The variants are not a menu: start with the preferred version and move only as far as the deal requires.

The clauses are drafting blocks, not complete agreements. They assume the definitions and interpretation provisions in the Bramber MSA. If a clause is used in a different document, check that the defined terms exist and that the cross-references point to the right place.

The guidance note under each clause explains the commercial point, the usual counterparty objection and the boundary of the fallback. It is not legal advice for a specific deal; the playbook position and the approval matrix still apply.
1.	Select the clause that matches the topic and contract type. Do not combine variants from different clauses without checking the interaction.
2.	Check the defined terms. If the counterparty uses 'Services', 'Fees' or 'Customer Data' differently, conform the clause before sending it.
3.	Use the preferred variant unless the playbook records a fallback for the deal. If you use a fallback, note the clause ID and variant in the deal summary.
4.	Do not use a fallback that has not been approved for the contract type. A fallback in an MSA may not be available in an order form.
5.	Send any new variant to Tom Whitlock for review before it goes into the library.

Subject to Clause 11.3 (Exclusions), each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The parties agree that this limitation is a reasonable allocation of risk having regard to the Fees, the nature of the Services and the availability of insurance.

Subject to Clause 11.3, each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twenty-four (24) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim, provided that liability for breach of Clause 8 (Data Protection) shall not exceed two times the Fees paid or payable in the preceding twelve (12) months.

Subject to Clause 11.3, Supplier's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) £1,000,000. Customer's aggregate liability shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable in the same period. The floor in (b) applies only where it does not exceed two times the annual Fees. The parties acknowledge that the floors are intended to cover the cost of a serious service failure and are not a penalty.

The cap is the commercial heart of the deal. The preferred version is mutual and measured on fees, which keeps it proportionate as the account grows. Fallback 1 is for enterprise deals where the customer's procurement team will not accept a 12-month cap; the data protection super-cap is the part to watch. Fallback 2 is a floor for smaller deals where a fee-based cap would be trivially low. Never accept a cap that applies only to Bramber or an uncapped data protection category.

Supplier owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Platform, the Documentation, the Supplier Tools, the Supplier Background IP and all Intellectual Property Rights in them, including any improvements, modifications or derivative works made during the Term. Customer owns all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data. Subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Supplier assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in the bespoke Deliverables identified in Schedule 1, excluding the Supplier Tools and Supplier Background IP. Supplier grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use the Supplier Background IP embedded in the Deliverables solely as necessary to use them for Customer's internal business purposes.

Supplier grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable right to use the Deliverables for Customer's internal business purposes during the Term, and a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use the Supplier Background IP embedded in the Deliverables after termination. Supplier retains ownership of the Platform, the Supplier Tools and the Supplier Background IP.

The parties jointly own the bespoke Deliverables, with each party free to use, license and exploit them without accounting to the other. Supplier retains sole ownership of the Platform, the Supplier Tools and all improvements to them, and Customer retains sole ownership of Customer Data.

The important boundary is between the deliverable and the tools used to make it. The preferred version follows playbook IND-02: the customer owns bespoke Deliverables once paid for, while Bramber keeps the Platform and background IP. Fallback 1 is a licence-only compromise for customers that will not accept an assignment. Fallback 2 is a last resort: joint ownership sounds generous but creates practical problems on exit. Never assign the Platform or model weights.

The parties shall comply with the Data Processing Agreement attached as Schedule 4. Customer is the controller and Supplier is the processor of Customer Personal Data. Supplier shall process Customer Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions, for the purposes described in Schedule 4, and shall implement the technical and organisational measures set out in that schedule.

Supplier shall process Customer Personal Data as a processor in accordance with Customer's written instructions and Applicable Data Protection Law. The parties shall enter into Customer's standard data processing agreement, provided that it does not impose obligations on Supplier that are inconsistent with this Agreement or the Security Schedule.

Where Customer's standard data processing agreement is required by a regulator or a sector-specific rule, the parties shall negotiate it in good faith and shall not unreasonably withhold or delay agreement. Pending execution, Supplier shall process Customer Personal Data in accordance with the security schedule and Applicable Data Protection Law.

A DPA is not optional where personal data is processed. The preferred version incorporates our schedule and keeps the role allocation clear. Fallback 1 is common in enterprise deals; the proviso is doing the work, because customer DPAs often contain audit and liability terms that conflict with the MSA. Fallback 2 is a bridging position for regulated customers and should always have a dated completion milestone.

Each party shall keep the other's Confidential Information confidential, use it only for the purposes of this Agreement, and disclose it only to its personnel and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Clause. These obligations survive for three (3) years after termination, except for trade secrets, which are protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.

The confidentiality obligations in this Clause survive for five (5) years after termination. The parties acknowledge that the duration reflects the sensitivity of the information and does not extend to information that enters the public domain without breach.

Each party may disclose the other's Confidential Information to its Affiliates and to bona fide prospective investors or acquirers, provided that the recipient is bound by a written confidentiality undertaking and the disclosing party is notified before disclosure. The disclosing party remains responsible for any breach by a recipient.

Five years is the usual customer ask and is an acceptable fallback for MSA confidentiality. Do not accept perpetual confidentiality for ordinary commercial information; it is not credible and it makes the carve-outs harder to operate. Fallback 2 is an addition, not a replacement, and belongs in the representatives clause rather than the survival clause.

Customer may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, audit Supplier's compliance with this Agreement during normal business hours. The audit shall be conducted remotely where possible, shall not interfere with Supplier's operations, and shall be limited to the records and systems relevant to the Services. The auditor shall be independent and bound by confidentiality, and shall not have access to any other customer's data. Customer shall bear the cost of the audit unless the audit reveals a material discrepancy of more than five per cent (5%) in the Fees or a material breach of the Security Schedule.

Customer may audit Supplier twice in any twelve (12) month period on at least fifteen (15) Business Days' prior written notice, subject to a maximum of five (5) auditor days per audit. The audit shall be conducted remotely unless Customer's regulator requires an on-site visit. The parties shall share the cost of an audit that is inconclusive.

Where Customer is a regulated entity, Customer's regulator may examine Supplier's records relevant to the Services on reasonable notice, subject to confidentiality and a scope agreed in advance. Supplier shall cooperate with the examination but shall not be required to provide access to any other customer's data or to its source code.

The audit clause is an operational commitment, so the scope matters more than the frequency. Keep the audit remote-first and cap the auditor days. Fallback 2 is for financial services and health customers whose regulator has statutory examination powers; it is narrower than a general audit right and should be described as such.

Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience after the first twelve (12) months of the Subscription Term on ninety (90) days' written notice, provided that Customer pays all Fees accrued to the effective date of termination and any non-cancellable third-party commitments incurred by Supplier before the notice. Supplier has no right to terminate for convenience.

Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience on sixty (60) days' written notice at any time after the first twelve (12) months, subject to an early termination charge equal to the Fees that would have been payable for the remainder of the then-current twelve (12) month period, discounted to present value.

Customer may terminate the affected Order Form for convenience after the first twelve (12) months on ninety (90) days' written notice where Customer ceases to operate the business unit to which the Services relate or is required to do so by a change in Applicable Law, paying the Fees for the notice period and any non-cancellable third-party commitments. The termination right does not apply to a reorganisation, a change of control or a transfer of the Services to an Affiliate.

The preferred version gives the customer a clean exit after year one while protecting the committed year. Fallback 1 is a commercial compromise: the early termination charge is the number to negotiate, not the notice period. Fallback 2 is a narrow exit for genuine business discontinuation; it should not be widened to cover ordinary budget pressure.

Customer shall pay the Fees set out in the Order Form within thirty (30) days of the date of Supplier's invoice. Fees are exclusive of VAT and any other applicable taxes, which shall be paid by Customer. Customer shall notify Supplier of any disputed amount within ten (10) Business Days of the invoice date and shall pay all undisputed amounts when due. Late payment shall attract interest at four per cent (4%) above the Bank of England base rate.

Customer shall pay undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date. Customer may withhold payment of a disputed amount pending resolution, provided that the dispute is notified within ten (10) Business Days and the undisputed balance is paid on time.

Customer shall pay invoices within sixty (60) days of the invoice date where Customer is a public authority or a regulated entity subject to a statutory payment policy. Supplier may suspend the Services on thirty (30) days' written notice if undisputed Fees remain unpaid for more than sixty (60) days.

Payment terms are working capital, not a legal nicety. The preferred position is 30 days from invoice date, not from receipt. Fallback 2 is for public-sector customers whose payment cycle is set by statute; the suspension right is what makes the longer term tolerable. Never accept pay-when-paid or payment on customer acceptance.

Supplier shall make the Production Environment available at least 99.9% of the time in each calendar month, excluding Scheduled Maintenance notified at least five (5) Business Days in advance. If Supplier fails to meet the Availability Commitment, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit calculated in accordance with Schedule 3. Service credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for the failure and shall not exceed fifteen per cent (15%) of the monthly Fees in aggregate.

Supplier shall make the Production Environment available at least 99.5% of the time in each calendar month. Service credits shall be calculated on a sliding scale and shall not exceed twenty-five per cent (25%) of the monthly Fees. Customer may terminate the affected Order Form if Availability falls below 99.5% for three (3) consecutive calendar months.

Where Customer requires a higher Availability Commitment for a business-critical service, the parties shall agree a separate service level schedule and the Fees shall be adjusted to reflect the additional resilience, monitoring and support required. Credits for the enhanced service shall be capped at the Fees attributable to that service.

Credits are a price adjustment, not a penalty. The cap is more important than the percentage: an uncapped credit can wipe out a month's revenue and is effectively an unlimited liability. Fallback 2 is the right answer when a customer asks for 99.99%; it is a different service, not a different clause.

Supplier may appoint sub-processors to process Customer Personal Data in accordance with the Data Processing Agreement. Supplier shall maintain a current list of sub-processors, notify Customer of any addition or replacement at least thirty (30) days in advance, and give Customer a right to object on reasonable data protection grounds. Supplier remains liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors as if they were its own.

Supplier shall obtain Customer's prior written consent to the appointment of any new sub-processor, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed and deemed given if Customer does not object within ten (10) Business Days. Supplier may appoint its Affiliates and its existing infrastructure providers without consent.

Supplier may appoint sub-processors where necessary to provide the Services, provided that the sub-processor is bound by written terms no less protective than this Agreement and the Data Processing Agreement. Supplier shall notify Customer of any sub-processor that processes Customer Personal Data outside the UK or EEA before the transfer begins.

General authorisation with notice and objection is the workable model. Prior consent for every change is acceptable only with a deemed-approval mechanism and a carve-out for affiliates and existing infrastructure. The flow-down obligation in Fallback 2 is a floor, not a substitute for the notice and objection right.
Use for: MSA; Order Form; NDA

This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by the laws of England and Wales. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales. Before commencing proceedings, the parties shall escalate the dispute to their respective senior representatives, who shall meet within ten (10) Business Days and attempt in good faith to resolve it for a further twenty (20) Business Days.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware. The escalation procedure in Clause 18.3 applies before any proceedings, except for applications for injunctive relief.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Munich. The English language version of this Agreement prevails over any translation. The escalation procedure in Clause 18.3 applies before any proceedings.

English law is the default because our contracts, insurance and counsel are English. Delaware is the usual US compromise and is acceptable for US customers. German law is available for German customers where the DPA or the customer's public-sector status requires it; check that the liability and audit positions still work under German law before using Fallback 2.
CL-11  Assignment and change of control

Neither party may assign, novate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights under it without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, provided that the assignee assumes the assigning party's obligations in writing and the other party is notified within thirty (30) days.

Supplier may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all of its assets without consent. Customer may assign to an Affiliate without consent, but may not assign to a competitor of Supplier without Supplier's prior written consent.

Customer may terminate this Agreement on sixty (60) days' written notice if Supplier is acquired by a direct competitor of Customer, provided that the notice is given within thirty (30) days of the acquisition and Customer pays all Fees accrued to the effective date of termination.

A change-of-control termination right is a financing risk. Fallback 2 is acceptable only for a named competitor list and a narrow window; do not accept a general right to terminate on any change of control. The notification obligation in the preferred version is what gives the other party visibility without a veto.

Neither party shall use the other party's name, logo or trademarks in any press release, advertisement, case study or public communication without the other party's prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Supplier may include Customer's name in a confidential list of reference customers provided to prospective customers under a written confidentiality obligation.

Supplier may publish an anonymised case study describing the Services and the results achieved, provided that Customer has approved the facts and any quotation in writing before publication. Customer may withdraw approval on thirty (30) days' written notice.

The parties shall issue a joint press release on execution in a form approved by both parties. Neither party shall make any other public statement about the relationship without the other's prior written consent, except as required by law or by the rules of a recognised stock exchange.

References are valuable, but consent is the default. The confidential reference list in the preferred version is usually enough for Sales. Fallback 1 is for customers who want to control the narrative; the withdrawal right is the concession. Fallback 2 is for listed customers whose announcement obligations are driven by market rules.

data.contentText: The confidentiality obligations in this Clause survive for five (5) years after termination. The parties acknowledge that the duration reflects the sensitivity of the information and does not extend to information that enters the public domain without breach.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: Each party may disclose the other's Confidential Information to its Affiliates and to bona fide prospective investors or acquirers, provided that the recipient is bound by a written confidentiality undertaking and the disclosing party is notified before disclosure. The disclosing party remains responsible for any breach by a recipient.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: Five years is the usual customer ask and is an acceptable fallback for MSA confidentiality. Do not accept perpetual confidentiality for ordinary commercial information; it is not credible and it makes the carve-outs harder to operate. Fallback 2 is an addition, not a replacement, and belongs in the representatives clause rather than the survival clause.

data.title: CL-05  Audit rights
data.contentText: Use for: MSA; DPA

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: Customer may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, audit Supplier's compliance with this Agreement during normal business hours. The audit shall be conducted remotely where possible, shall not interfere with Supplier's operations, and shall be limited to the records and systems relevant to the Services. The auditor shall be independent and bound by confidentiality, and shall not have access to any other customer's data. Customer shall bear the cost of the audit unless the audit reveals a material discrepancy of more than five per cent (5%) in the Fees or a material breach of the Security Schedule.

data.title: FALLBACK 1
data.contentText: Customer may audit Supplier twice in any twelve (12) month period on at least fifteen (15) Business Days' prior written notice, subject to a maximum of five (5) auditor days per audit. The audit shall be conducted remotely unless Customer's regulator requires an on-site visit. The parties shall share the cost of an audit that is inconclusive.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: Where Customer is a regulated entity, Customer's regulator may examine Supplier's records relevant to the Services on reasonable notice, subject to confidentiality and a scope agreed in advance. Supplier shall cooperate with the examination but shall not be required to provide access to any other customer's data or to its source code.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: The audit clause is an operational commitment, so the scope matters more than the frequency. Keep the audit remote-first and cap the auditor days. Fallback 2 is for financial services and health customers whose regulator has statutory examination powers; it is narrower than a general audit right and should be described as such.

data.title: CL-06  Termination for convenience
data.contentText: Use for: MSA; Order Form

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience after the first twelve (12) months of the Subscription Term on ninety (90) days' written notice, provided that Customer pays all Fees accrued to the effective date of termination and any non-cancellable third-party commitments incurred by Supplier before the notice. Supplier has no right to terminate for convenience.

data.title: FALLBACK 1
data.contentText: Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience on sixty (60) days' written notice at any time after the first twelve (12) months, subject to an early termination charge equal to the Fees that would have been payable for the remainder of the then-current twelve (12) month period, discounted to present value.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: Customer may terminate the affected Order Form for convenience after the first twelve (12) months on ninety (90) days' written notice where Customer ceases to operate the business unit to which the Services relate or is required to do so by a change in Applicable Law, paying the Fees for the notice period and any non-cancellable third-party commitments. The termination right does not apply to a reorganisation, a change of control or a transfer of the Services to an Affiliate.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: The preferred version gives the customer a clean exit after year one while protecting the committed year. Fallback 1 is a commercial compromise: the early termination charge is the number to negotiate, not the notice period. Fallback 2 is a narrow exit for genuine business discontinuation; it should not be widened to cover ordinary budget pressure.

data.title: CL-07  Fees and payment
data.contentText: Use for: MSA; Order Form

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: Customer shall pay the Fees set out in the Order Form within thirty (30) days of the date of Supplier's invoice. Fees are exclusive of VAT and any other applicable taxes, which shall be paid by Customer. Customer shall notify Supplier of any disputed amount within ten (10) Business Days of the invoice date and shall pay all undisputed amounts when due. Late payment shall attract interest at four per cent (4%) above the Bank of England base rate.

data.title: FALLBACK 1
data.contentText: Customer shall pay undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date. Customer may withhold payment of a disputed amount pending resolution, provided that the dispute is notified within ten (10) Business Days and the undisputed balance is paid on time.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: Customer shall pay invoices within sixty (60) days of the invoice date where Customer is a public authority or a regulated entity subject to a statutory payment policy. Supplier may suspend the Services on thirty (30) days' written notice if undisputed Fees remain unpaid for more than sixty (60) days.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: Payment terms are working capital, not a legal nicety. The preferred position is 30 days from invoice date, not from receipt. Fallback 2 is for public-sector customers whose payment cycle is set by statute; the suspension right is what makes the longer term tolerable. Never accept pay-when-paid or payment on customer acceptance.

data.title: CL-08  Service levels and credits
data.contentText: Use for: Order Form; SOW

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: Supplier shall make the Production Environment available at least 99.9% of the time in each calendar month, excluding Scheduled Maintenance notified at least five (5) Business Days in advance. If Supplier fails to meet the Availability Commitment, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit calculated in accordance with Schedule 3. Service credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for the failure and shall not exceed fifteen per cent (15%) of the monthly Fees in aggregate.

data.title: FALLBACK 1
data.contentText: Supplier shall make the Production Environment available at least 99.5% of the time in each calendar month. Service credits shall be calculated on a sliding scale and shall not exceed twenty-five per cent (25%) of the monthly Fees. Customer may terminate the affected Order Form if Availability falls below 99.5% for three (3) consecutive calendar months.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: Where Customer requires a higher Availability Commitment for a business-critical service, the parties shall agree a separate service level schedule and the Fees shall be adjusted to reflect the additional resilience, monitoring and support required. Credits for the enhanced service shall be capped at the Fees attributable to that service.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: Credits are a price adjustment, not a penalty. The cap is more important than the percentage: an uncapped credit can wipe out a month's revenue and is effectively an unlimited liability. Fallback 2 is the right answer when a customer asks for 99.99%; it is a different service, not a different clause.

data.title: CL-09  Sub-processors and subcontracting
data.contentText: Use for: MSA; DPA

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: Supplier may appoint sub-processors to process Customer Personal Data in accordance with the Data Processing Agreement. Supplier shall maintain a current list of sub-processors, notify Customer of any addition or replacement at least thirty (30) days in advance, and give Customer a right to object on reasonable data protection grounds. Supplier remains liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors as if they were its own.

data.title: FALLBACK 1
data.contentText: Supplier shall obtain Customer's prior written consent to the appointment of any new sub-processor, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed and deemed given if Customer does not object within ten (10) Business Days. Supplier may appoint its Affiliates and its existing infrastructure providers without consent.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: Supplier may appoint sub-processors where necessary to provide the Services, provided that the sub-processor is bound by written terms no less protective than this Agreement and the Data Processing Agreement. Supplier shall notify Customer of any sub-processor that processes Customer Personal Data outside the UK or EEA before the transfer begins.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: General authorisation with notice and objection is the workable model. Prior consent for every change is acceptable only with a deemed-approval mechanism and a carve-out for affiliates and existing infrastructure. The flow-down obligation in Fallback 2 is a floor, not a substitute for the notice and objection right.

data.title: CL-10  Governing law and disputes
data.contentText: Use for: MSA; Order Form; NDA

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by the laws of England and Wales. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales. Before commencing proceedings, the parties shall escalate the dispute to their respective senior representatives, who shall meet within ten (10) Business Days and attempt in good faith to resolve it for a further twenty (20) Business Days.

data.title: FALLBACK 1
data.contentText: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware. The escalation procedure in Clause 18.3 applies before any proceedings, except for applications for injunctive relief.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Munich. The English language version of this Agreement prevails over any translation. The escalation procedure in Clause 18.3 applies before any proceedings.

data.title: GUIDANCE

data.title: CL-11  Assignment and change of control
data.contentText: Use for: MSA

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: Neither party may assign, novate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights under it without the other party's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, provided that the assignee assumes the assigning party's obligations in writing and the other party is notified within thirty (30) days.

data.title: FALLBACK 1
data.contentText: Supplier may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all of its assets without consent. Customer may assign to an Affiliate without consent, but may not assign to a competitor of Supplier without Supplier's prior written consent.

data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: Customer may terminate this Agreement on sixty (60) days' written notice if Supplier is acquired by a direct competitor of Customer, provided that the notice is given within thirty (30) days of the acquisition and Customer pays all Fees accrued to the effective date of termination.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: A change-of-control termination right is a financing risk. Fallback 2 is acceptable only for a named competitor list and a narrow window; do not accept a general right to terminate on any change of control. The notification obligation in the preferred version is what gives the other party visibility without a veto.

data.title: PREFERRED
data.contentText: Neither party shall use the other party's name, logo or trademarks in any press release, advertisement, case study or public communication without the other party's prior written consent. data.title: FALLBACK 2
data.contentText: The parties shall issue a joint press release on execution in a form approved by both parties. Neither party shall make any other public statement about the relationship without the other's prior written consent, except as required by law or by the rules of a recognised stock exchange.

data.title: GUIDANCE
data.contentText: References are valuable, but consent is the default. The confidential reference list in the preferred version is usually enough for Sales. data.text: Positions, fallbacks and approval routes for customer contracts
MSA, order forms, statements of work and related supply terms

This playbook is the default position for every commercial contract that Bramber Software Limited signs as supplier. It exists so that Sales, Finance and Legal start from the same answer, and so that a deviation is a decision rather than an accident.

It covers master services agreements, order forms and statements of work on customer paper, together with the supply-side terms that sit underneath them. It does not cover procurement contracts where Bramber is the customer, employment contracts, or leases. Those have separate guides.

The playbook is unashamedly commercial. A position is not a rule for its own sake: each one protects a specific exposure that we have priced, insured or accepted. If a counterparty asks for something different, the question is whether the exposure has moved, not whether the words have changed.
1.	Identify the contract type and the paper. Check whether the counterparty has supplied its own MSA, order form or SOW, or whether we are working from Bramber paper.
2.	Find the topic in the position tables. Each table has an Applies to row, so you can see at a glance whether the position governs an MSA, an order form, an SOW or more than one.
3.	Compare the clause in front of you with Our position. If it matches, record it as standard and move on. Do not redline for style.
4.	If it does not match, look at Fallback. A fallback is pre-approved for the stated contract type, subject to the approver named in the table. Record the deviation in the deal summary.
5.	If the clause reaches Walk-away, stop. Do not negotiate it in the room. Escalate to the named approver with the clause, the commercial context and the revenue at stake.

6.	If the topic is not in this playbook, treat it as UNADDRESSED and send it to the Legal Operations desk. Novel clauses are usually a signal that the counterparty is trying to solve a problem we have not seen; the answer is rarely to accept the first draft.
Every deviation is recorded under one of seven categories. The category drives the response and the approval route, so use the label rather than a free-text description.
What it means and what to do
The clause crosses a position we will not accept, or removes a protection the deal depends on. Do not sign without GC approval; the default answer is no.
The clause is outside our preferred position but within a documented fallback. Legal must redraft to the fallback and record the concession.
The clause is a fallback we have already approved for this contract type. Note it, but it does not need escalation.
A protection we require is absent. The risk is what the document does not say. Add the provision or obtain a written side letter.
The clause is capable of two or more reasonable readings, or uses a standard we cannot measure. Redraft to an objective test.
Two provisions in the same deal point in different directions. Resolve the conflict expressly; do not rely on an order of precedence clause to sort it out later.
The topic is outside this guide. Route to the Legal Operations desk for a written position before responding.
Approval is about the exposure, not the seniority of the person asking. If a deal triggers more than one row, obtain every approval before the document goes to signature.

Each table below is one topic. Read the Applies to row first; a position that governs an MSA does not automatically govern an order form or an SOW. Where a table says “—”, the row does not apply and no concession is available.
Position IDs are stable and are used in deal summaries and approval requests. Quote the ID, not the heading, when you escalate.

Aggregate liability under the agreement is capped at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months immediately before the event giving rise to the claim. The cap applies to each party, not only to Bramber.

24 months' fees where the customer's contract value is at least £250,000, or where the customer has required a higher cap in a competitive tender. A super-cap for data protection claims of 2x the annual fee is acceptable if the DPA is on our terms.
Uncapped liability, a cap above 2x annual fees, or a cap that applies only to Bramber. These are walk-away positions and require CFO and GC approval.
Tom Whitlock for the standard cap; Marcus Feld and Priya Raghavan for any increase.

The cap is the number the business has priced and insured. Anything above it is an uninsured exposure. Sample: “Each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.”

The only uncapped categories are death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, and breach of confidentiality. The IP indemnity is subject to the general cap, with a maximum of 2x the annual fee.

Uncapped liability for breach of confidentiality is acceptable where the customer's data is genuinely sensitive and the DPA contains a matching confidentiality obligation. Do not accept an uncapped data protection category.
Unlimited liability for breach of data protection law, regulatory fines, or “any breach of this Agreement”. These transfer an unquantifiable risk to Bramber and are not insurable on our programme.
Marcus Feld and Priya Raghavan for any change to the carve-outs.

Regulatory fines are not a commercial debt we can price. Our cyber policy responds to incident costs, not to a contractual indemnity for a regulator's penalty. Sample: “Nothing in this Clause limits either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, fraud, or breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality).”

Bramber owns the Platform, the Documentation, all background IP and every improvement to them, whether made before or during the engagement. The customer receives a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the Services for its internal business during the subscription term.
A perpetual licence to use configured elements of the Platform for the customer's internal business after termination, limited to the scope in the order form. No assignment of Platform IP.
Any transfer or assignment of Platform IP, source code, model weights or background IP to the customer. This is a walk-away position and requires GC and CTO approval.

The Platform is the asset the company is valued on. A customer-specific configuration is not a reason to transfer the underlying product. If a customer needs continuity, offer a licence and an escrow arrangement under UNA-01.
IND-02  Deliverables, customer data and feedback

The customer owns its Customer Data. Bramber assigns ownership of bespoke Deliverables (documents, reports and configured outputs) once paid for, excluding any Bramber background IP, tools, templates or know-how embedded in them. Feedback may be used royalty-free to improve the Services.
A broad licence to the Deliverables rather than an assignment, or joint ownership of bespoke materials with a perpetual licence back to Bramber.
An assignment of Deliverables that captures background IP, pre-existing tools or model improvements, or a restriction on using know-how and techniques developed on the engagement.
Tom Whitlock; Priya Raghavan if background IP is in scope.
The distinction between a deliverable and the factory that made it is the whole game. Draft the assignment with a schedule that lists the deliverables and expressly excludes background IP.

Bramber indemnifies the customer against third-party claims that the Services infringe IP rights, subject to the liability cap, prompt notice, sole control of the defence and the customer's obligation to stop using the Service after notice. The indemnity excludes modifications, combinations and customer data.
A separate indemnity cap of 2x annual fees, or a obligation to procure a licence or replace the affected functionality at Bramber's option.
An uncapped IP indemnity, an indemnity that covers customer modifications or third-party services, or one that survives without a time limit.
Tom Whitlock; Marcus Feld for any separate cap.
An IP claim is plausible in a crowded workflow market, but it is still a capped commercial risk. The exclusions are what make the indemnity underwritable.

An initial term of 12 to 36 months, renewing for successive 12-month periods unless either party gives at least 60 days' written notice before the end of the then-current term. No renewal period longer than 12 months.

A 90-day notice period, a 120-day period where the customer's budget cycle requires it and the account has a named renewal owner, or a 24-month renewal where the customer has committed to a minimum volume and the pricing reflects it.
Automatic renewal for more than 24 months, a notice period longer than 120 days, or a term that renews indefinitely without a termination right.
Tom Whitlock; Nadia Iqbal for any renewal term longer than 12 months.
Long notice periods look harmless until the account team misses the diary entry. 60 days gives Sales a full quarter to renew; 120 days hands the customer a free option.

The customer may terminate an order form for convenience after the first 12 months on 90 days' written notice, paying fees for the notice period and any non-cancellable third-party commitments. Bramber has no termination for convenience right.
Termination for convenience on 60 days' notice with an early termination charge equal to the fees for the remainder of the then-current 12-month period, or a one-time 10% buy-out.
Termination for convenience in the first 12 months, or on less than 60 days' notice without a termination charge.
Nadia Iqbal and Tom Whitlock; Marcus Feld for any waiver of the termination charge.
A customer convenience right is a revenue risk, not a legal one. The notice period and charge are how we keep the committed ARR meaningful.
TER-03  Termination for cause and exit

Either party may terminate for material breach after 30 days' written notice and failure to cure, or immediately on insolvency. On exit, Bramber provides 90 days of transition assistance at standard rates and returns Customer Data in a common format.
A 15-day cure period for payment breaches and 60 days for other breaches; transition assistance for 60 days at cost.
Termination for any breach without a cure right, termination on a customer's insolvency without a right to suspend, or no exit assistance obligation at all.
Cure periods protect us from losing a contract over an invoicing dispute. Exit assistance is what stops a customer using data hostage as a negotiation tactic.

Invoices are payable within 30 days of the invoice date, in pounds sterling or the currency stated in the order form. Disputed amounts must be notified within 10 Business Days; undisputed amounts remain payable. Late payment interest is 4% above the Bank of England base rate.
45 days for UK customers, 60 days for large enterprise or public-sector customers, provided the customer has a purchase-order process that does not delay payment.
90 days or more, payment on customer acceptance, pay-when-paid, or a right to set off disputed amounts without a cap.
Marcus Feld for terms beyond 45 days.
Payment terms are working capital. A 60-day term on a £500,000 contract is a £40,000 financing cost we have not priced.
Fees may increase on each renewal by the lower of CPI plus 3% or 5%, on at least 60 days' written notice. Multi-year order forms may fix the increase at 3% per year.
A fixed 5% annual uplift, or a cap at CPI plus 4% where CPI is the published UK index.
Fees fixed for the whole term beyond 24 months with no uplift, or an uncapped increase above 8% in any year.
A price hold is a discount with a delay. If Sales wants a longer hold, it should be priced into year one, not discovered at renewal.

Travel and expenses are pre-approved in writing, charged at cost with receipts, and capped at 5% of the professional services fees for the engagement. Third-party licence costs are passed through at cost with evidence of the supplier invoice.
A fixed expenses allowance built into the fee, or a cap of 10% where the customer cannot pre-approve individual trips. Third-party licence cost increases above 10% require a change order.
Uncapped expenses, no pre-approval requirement, or an obligation to absorb third-party licence cost increases above 10% without a change order.
Tom Whitlock; Marcus Feld for any cap above 10%.

Expenses are a pass-through, not a profit centre, but they are also the line item customers dispute most often. A pre-approval and a cap keep both sides honest. Sample: “Customer shall reimburse pre-approved travel and expenses at cost, supported by receipts, up to five per cent (5%) of the Professional Services Fees.”

The customer may audit Bramber's compliance with the agreement once in any 12-month period, on at least 30 days' written notice, during business hours and remotely where possible. The auditor must be independent, bound by confidentiality and have no access to other customers' data. The customer bears the cost unless the audit reveals a material discrepancy of more than 5%.
Twice in any 12-month period for regulated customers, with 15 Business Days' notice; a maximum of five auditor days per audit; costs shared where the audit is inconclusive.
Audits on less than 5 Business Days' notice, unlimited frequency, unfettered access to systems or sub-processors, or audits at Bramber's cost regardless of outcome.

Audit clauses are operational commitments disguised as legal text. Every additional audit day is a cost the delivery team carries. Sample: “Customer may, no more than once in any twelve-month period and on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, audit Supplier's compliance with this Agreement during normal business hours.”

Bramber maintains ISO 27001 certification and a SOC 2 Type II report, and will provide the current report under NDA. Security measures are set out in the DPA or security schedule. Penetration testing by the customer requires prior written consent, a defined scope and a mutually agreed window.
A customer security questionnaire and a completed CAIQ, plus annual summary evidence. A single customer-commissioned penetration test per year at the customer's cost.
A right to conduct unannounced penetration testing, to access production systems, or to require remediation of findings outside the agreed severity thresholds.
Our certifications answer most of the questionnaire. Unrestricted testing rights create operational risk and can invalidate our own assurance position.

99.9% monthly availability for the production environment, measured excluding scheduled maintenance notified 5 Business Days in advance. Service credits are the sole remedy, calculated as a percentage of the monthly fee and capped at 15% of the monthly fee in aggregate.
99.5% availability with credits capped at 25% of the monthly fee, or a right to terminate after three consecutive months below the threshold.
Availability commitments above 99.95% without a corresponding change to the architecture and support model, uncapped credits, or a right to terminate for a single missed target.
Jonas Reed and Tom Whitlock; Marcus Feld for any credit cap above 25%.
The SLA is a promise about engineering, not a marketing line. Credits are a price adjustment, not a penalty, and must be capped.

Mutual confidentiality for the term and 3 years after termination. Standard carve-outs for public information, independently developed information, information received from a third party and disclosures required by law. No residuals clause. Return or destruction on request, with a certification.
A 5-year survival period; a 7-year survival period for trade secrets. A residuals clause limited to unaided memory and excluding any intentional memorisation.
Perpetual confidentiality, a residuals clause that permits use of disclosed information, or a restriction on hiring generally rather than targeted solicitation.
Confidentiality is cheap to give and expensive to police. The carve-outs do the real work; a perpetual obligation is not credible and creates a compliance burden.

Bramber warrants that the Services will perform materially in accordance with the Documentation and that professional services will be performed with reasonable skill and care. The remedy is repair or re-performance within 30 days. Acceptance is deemed 10 Business Days after delivery unless the customer gives a written notice specifying a material non-conformity.
A 90-day warranty period for professional services; a 15 Business Day deemed acceptance period; a right to reject only for material non-conformity against written acceptance criteria.
A warranty of fitness for a particular purpose, a warranty of uninterrupted or error-free operation, or acceptance at the customer's sole discretion with no deemed acceptance.
Tom Whitlock; Hannah Voss for any product warranty.
“Error-free” is not a warranty any software company can give. Acceptance criteria must be objective and tied to the SOW, or the project has no end date.

Indemnities are mutual, specific and subject to the liability cap. Bramber indemnifies for third-party IP infringement; the customer indemnifies for Customer Data, unlawful use and breach of its own obligations. Each indemnity is subject to prompt notice, sole control of the defence and reasonable cooperation.
A customer indemnity limited to third-party claims arising from Customer Data, with a cap equal to the fees paid in the preceding 12 months.
An uncapped indemnity, an indemnity for the customer's own negligence, or an obligation to defend claims that are outside the scope of the Services.
Tom Whitlock; Priya Raghavan for any uncapped indemnity.
An indemnity is a promise to stand behind a specific risk. If it is not specific, it is a second liability cap with worse words.

Bramber maintains professional indemnity of £10m, cyber liability of £10m, public liability of £5m and employer's liability of £5m, and will provide certificates on request. Insurance is not a substitute for the liability cap.
£5m professional indemnity and £5m cyber for mid-market customers; certificates annually rather than on every request.
A requirement to name the customer as an additional insured, to provide primary and non-contributory cover, or to maintain cover above £10m.
Insurance requirements are proxy liability caps. Adding a customer as an insured gives them a direct claim on our policy and complicates renewals.

Bramber may use affiliates and vetted sub-processors, with a current list in the DPA and a general authorisation to appoint replacements on 30 days' notice. Bramber remains liable for their performance. The customer may object on reasonable data protection grounds.
Prior written consent for new sub-processors, not unreasonably withheld or delayed, with a deemed approval after 10 Business Days.
Absolute customer consent for each sub-processor, a right to veto the use of cloud infrastructure providers, or a requirement that Bramber's affiliates be treated as third parties.
Our service runs on third-party infrastructure. A veto right over sub-processors is a veto right over the product roadmap.
ASG-01  Assignment and change of control

Neither party may assign the agreement without the other's written consent, except to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes the obligations in writing.
Customer consent for Bramber's assignment to a competitor of the customer, but not for a change of control of Bramber.
A right for the customer to terminate on any change of control of Bramber, or a prohibition on assignment to an affiliate.
Investors and acquirers need a clean assignment path. A change-of-control termination right turns a financing event into a customer churn event.

English law, with the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales. Before litigation, the parties escalate to senior representatives for 20 Business Days. Either party may seek injunctive relief at any time.
Delaware or New York law for US customers, with courts in those states; German law for German customers where the DPA requires it. Escalation remains mandatory.
The customer's local courts with no escalation, arbitration in a jurisdiction where we have no presence, or a requirement to litigate in more than one forum.
Tom Whitlock; Priya Raghavan for any non-English law.
We are an English company with English insurance and English counsel. A US law clause is manageable; a US court clause with no escalation is an expense we do not need.

A party is excused from performance for events beyond its reasonable control, excluding payment obligations. The affected party must notify promptly and mitigate. Either party may terminate if the event continues for 60 days.
A 90-day termination threshold for infrastructure failures, provided the customer receives a service credit for the affected period.
Force majeure that excuses payment, or an exclusion that captures failures of our own sub-processors.
Force majeure is for events neither party can control. It is not a cure for a supplier's capacity problem.

Neither party may use the other's name, logo or trademarks without prior written consent, except that Bramber may include the customer's name in a confidential reference list shared with prospective customers under NDA.
An anonymised case study with agreed facts and a quote approved by the customer; a press release jointly approved.
A blanket prohibition on referring to the customer as a customer, or a right for the customer to approve all future marketing generally.
References are the cheapest form of proof we have. A blanket ban is usually a procurement default, not a real concern.
CUS-01  Customer obligations and acceptable use

The customer is responsible for the accuracy and lawfulness of Customer Data, for its users' compliance with the acceptable use policy, and for maintaining its own systems and connectivity. Prohibited uses are listed objectively: unlawful content, malware, unauthorised access, excessive load and use to build a competing product.
A customer-specific acceptable use schedule for regulated customers, provided it does not impose obligations on Bramber beyond the DPA and security schedule.
An obligation for Bramber to monitor Customer Data for unlawful content, or a customer right to suspend fees because of a third party's use of the Service.
We are a processor, not an insurer of our customers' conduct. The acceptable use policy should be specific enough to enforce and narrow enough to operate.
MSA; Order Form; SOW; DPA; NDA

Any clause that does not map to a position in this playbook is treated as novel. Examples: AI or model-training rights, benchmarking, ESG or modern slavery audits, source code escrow, most-favoured-customer pricing, regulatory examination rights, and customer-specific service levels. The default answer is no until Legal has written a position.
A time-limited pilot or side letter that isolates the novel obligation, with a documented owner and an exit date.
A novel obligation that is uncapped, perpetual, or impossible to operationalise. Do not accept it simply because the revenue is strategic.

Novel clauses are where the playbook earns its keep. They are usually drafted for a different business model and import obligations we cannot meet. The correct response is a written position, not a redline in the room.

data.title: Commercial Contracts Playbook
data.contentText:
Commercial Contracts Playbook
Positions, fallbacks and approval routes for customer contracts
4.2 | Priya Raghavan, General Counsel | 14 January 2026 | Internal — Legal & Commercial | MSA, order forms, statements of work and related supply terms

data.title: Purpose
data.contentText:
This playbook is the default position for every commercial contract that Bramber Software Limited signs as supplier. It exists so that Sales, Finance and Legal start from the same answer, and so that a deviation is a decision rather than an accident.
It covers master services agreements, order forms and statements of work on customer paper, together with the supply-side terms that sit underneath them. It does not cover procurement contracts where Bramber is the customer, employment contracts, or leases. Those have separate guides.
The playbook is unashamedly commercial. A position is not a rule for its own sake: each one protects a specific exposure that we have priced, insured or accepted. If a counterparty asks for something different, the question is whether the exposure has moved, not whether the words have changed.

data.title: How to use this playbook
data.contentText:
1.	Identify the contract type and the paper. Check whether the counterparty has supplied its own MSA, order form or SOW, or whether we are working from Bramber paper.
2.	Find the topic in the position tables. Each table has an Applies to row, so you can see at a glance whether the position governs an MSA, an order form, an SOW or more than one.
3.	Compare the clause in front of you with Our position. If it matches, record it as standard and move on. Do not redline for style.
4.	If it does not match, look at Fallback. A fallback is pre-approved for the stated contract type, subject to the approver named in the table. Record the deviation in the deal summary.
5.	If the clause reaches Walk-away, stop. Do not negotiate it in the room. Escalate to the named approver with the clause, the commercial context and the revenue at stake.
6.	If the topic is not in this playbook, treat it as UNADDRESSED and send it to the Legal Operations desk. Novel clauses are usually a signal that the counterparty is trying to solve a problem we have not seen; the answer is rarely to accept the first draft.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: Every deviation is recorded under one of seven categories. The category drives the response and the approval route, so use the label rather than a free-text description.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: WALK_AWAY_BREACH | The clause crosses a position we will not accept, or removes a protection the deal depends on. Do not sign without GC approval; the default answer is no.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: NEEDS_FALLBACK | The clause is outside our preferred position but within a documented fallback. Legal must redraft to the fallback and record the concession.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: ACCEPTABLE_FALLBACK | The clause is a fallback we have already approved for this contract type. Note it, but it does not need escalation.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: MISSING_PROVISION | A protection we require is absent. The risk is what the document does not say. Add the provision or obtain a written side letter.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: AMBIGUOUS | The clause is capable of two or more reasonable readings, or uses a standard we cannot measure. Redraft to an objective test.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: CROSS_CLAUSE_CONFLICT | Two provisions in the same deal point in different directions. Resolve the conflict expressly; do not rely on an order of precedence clause to sort it out later.

data.title: Deviation categories
data.contentText: UNADDRESSED_BY_PLAYBOOK | The topic is outside this guide. Route to the Legal Operations desk for a written position before responding.

data.title: Approval matrix
data.contentText: Approval is about the exposure, not the seniority of the person asking. If a deal triggers more than one row, obtain every approval before the document goes to signature.

data.title: Position tables
data.contentText:
Each table below is one topic. Read the Applies to row first; a position that governs an MSA does not automatically govern an order form or an SOW. Where a table says “—”, the row does not apply and no concession is available.
Position IDs are stable and are used in deal summaries and approval requests. Quote the ID, not the heading, when you escalate.

data.title: LIA-01  Liability cap
data.contentText: LIA-01 | MSA; Order Form | Aggregate liability under the agreement is capped at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months immediately before the event giving rise to the claim. The cap applies to each party, not only to Bramber. | 24 months' fees where the customer's contract value is at least £250,000, or where the customer has required a higher cap in a competitive tender. A super-cap for data protection claims of 2x the annual fee is acceptable if the DPA is on our terms. | Uncapped liability, a cap above 2x annual fees, or a cap that applies only to Bramber. These are walk-away positions and require CFO and GC approval. | Tom Whitlock for the standard cap; Marcus Feld and Priya Raghavan for any increase. | The cap is the number the business has priced and insured. Anything above it is an uninsured exposure. Sample: “Each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.”

data.title: LIA-02  Unlimited liability and carve-outs
data.contentText: LIA-02 | MSA; Order Form | The only uncapped categories are death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, and breach of confidentiality. The IP indemnity is subject to the general cap, with a maximum of 2x the annual fee. | Uncapped liability for breach of confidentiality is acceptable where the customer's data is genuinely sensitive and the DPA contains a matching confidentiality obligation. Do not accept an uncapped data protection category. | Unlimited liability for breach of data protection law, regulatory fines, or “any breach of this Agreement”. These transfer an unquantifiable risk to Bramber and are not insurable on our programme. | Marcus Feld and Priya Raghavan for any change to the carve-outs. | Regulatory fines are not a commercial debt we can price. Our cyber policy responds to incident costs, not to a contractual indemnity for a regulator's penalty. Sample: “Nothing in this Clause limits either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, fraud, or breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality).”

data.title: IND-01  Platform and background IP
data.contentText: IND-01 | MSA; SOW | Bramber owns the Platform, the Documentation, all background IP and every improvement to them, whether made before or during the engagement. The customer receives a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the Services for its internal business during the subscription term. | A perpetual licence to use configured elements of the Platform for the customer's internal business after termination, limited to the scope in the order form. No assignment of Platform IP. | Any transfer or assignment of Platform IP, source code, model weights or background IP to the customer. This is a walk-away position and requires GC and CTO approval. | Priya Raghavan and Hannah Voss. | The Platform is the asset the company is valued on. A customer-specific configuration is not a reason to transfer the underlying product. If a customer needs continuity, offer a licence and an escrow arrangement under UNA-01.

data.title: IND-02  Deliverables, customer data and feedback
IND-02  Deliverables, customer data and feedback
data.contentText: IND-02 | MSA; SOW | The customer owns its Customer Data. Bramber assigns ownership of bespoke Deliverables (documents, reports and configured outputs) once paid for, excluding any Bramber background IP, tools, templates or know-how embedded in them. Feedback may be used royalty-free to improve the Services. | A broad licence to the Deliverables rather than an assignment, or joint ownership of bespoke materials with a perpetual licence back to Bramber. | An assignment of Deliverables that captures background IP, pre-existing tools or model improvements, or a restriction on using know-how and techniques developed on the engagement. | Tom Whitlock; Priya Raghavan if background IP is in scope. | The distinction between a deliverable and the factory that made it is the whole game. Draft the assignment with a schedule that lists the deliverables and expressly excludes background IP.

data.title: IND-03  IP indemnity
data.contentText: IND-03 | MSA; Order Form | Bramber indemnifies the customer against third-party claims that the Services infringe IP rights, subject to the liability cap, prompt notice, sole control of the defence and the customer's obligation to stop using the Service after notice. The indemnity excludes modifications, combinations and customer data. | A separate indemnity cap of 2x annual fees, or a obligation to procure a licence or replace the affected functionality at Bramber's option. | An uncapped IP indemnity, an indemnity that covers customer modifications or third-party services, or one that survives without a time limit. | Tom Whitlock; Marcus Feld for any separate cap. | An IP claim is plausible in a crowded workflow market, but it is still a capped commercial risk. The exclusions are what make the indemnity underwritable.

data.title: TER-01  Term, renewal and notice
data.contentText: TER-01 | MSA; Order Form | An initial term of 12 to 36 months, renewing for successive 12-month periods unless either party gives at least 60 days' written notice before the end of the then-current term. No renewal period longer than 12 months. | A 90-day notice period, a 120-day period where the customer's budget cycle requires it and the account has a named renewal owner, or a 24-month renewal where the customer has committed to a minimum volume and the pricing reflects it. | Automatic renewal for more than 24 months, a notice period longer than 120 days, or a term that renews indefinitely without a termination right. | Tom Whitlock; Nadia Iqbal for any renewal term longer than 12 months. | Long notice periods look harmless until the account team misses the diary entry. 60 days gives Sales a full quarter to renew; 120 days hands the customer a free option.

data.title: TER-02  Termination for convenience
data.contentText: TER-02 | MSA; Order Form | The customer may terminate an order form for convenience after the first 12 months on 90 days' written notice, paying fees for the notice period and any non-cancellable third-party commitments. Bramber has no termination for convenience right. | Termination for convenience on 60 days' notice with an early termination charge equal to the fees for the remainder of the then-current 12-month period, or a one-time 10% buy-out. | Termination for convenience in the first 12 months, or on less than 60 days' notice without a termination charge. | Nadia Iqbal and Tom Whitlock; Marcus Feld for any waiver of the termination charge. | A customer convenience right is a revenue risk, not a legal one. The notice period and charge are how we keep the committed ARR meaningful.

data.title: TER-03  Termination for cause and exit
TER-03  Termination for cause and exit
data.contentText: TER-03 | MSA; SOW | Either party may terminate for material breach after 30 days' written notice and failure to cure, or immediately on insolvency. On exit, Bramber provides 90 days of transition assistance at standard rates and returns Customer Data in a common format. | A 15-day cure period for payment breaches and 60 days for other breaches; transition assistance for 60 days at cost. | Termination for any breach without a cure right, termination on a customer's insolvency without a right to suspend, or no exit assistance obligation at all. | Tom Whitlock. | Cure periods protect us from losing a contract over an invoicing dispute. Exit assistance is what stops a customer using data hostage as a negotiation tactic.

data.title: PAY-01  Payment terms
data.contentText: PAY-01 | MSA; Order Form | Invoices are payable within 30 days of the invoice date, in pounds sterling or the currency stated in the order form. Disputed amounts must be notified within 10 Business Days; undisputed amounts remain payable. Late payment interest is 4% above the Bank of England base rate. | 45 days for UK customers, 60 days for large enterprise or public-sector customers, provided the customer has a purchase-order process that does not delay payment. | 90 days or more, payment on customer acceptance, pay-when-paid, or a right to set off disputed amounts without a cap. | Marcus Feld for terms beyond 45 days. | Payment terms are working capital. A 60-day term on a £500,000 contract is a £40,000 financing cost we have not priced.

data.contentText: PAY-02 | MSA; Order Form | Fees may increase on each renewal by the lower of CPI plus 3% or 5%, on at least 60 days' written notice. If Sales wants a longer hold, it should be priced into year one, not discovered at renewal.

data.title: INS-01  Insurance
data.contentText: INS-01 | MSA | Bramber maintains professional indemnity of £10m, cyber liability of £10m, public liability of £5m and employer's liability of £5m, and will provide certificates on request. Insurance is not a substitute for the liability cap. | £5m professional indemnity and £5m cyber for mid-market customers; certificates annually rather than on every request. | A requirement to name the customer as an additional insured, to provide primary and non-contributory cover, or to maintain cover above £10m. | Marcus Feld. | Insurance requirements are proxy liability caps. Adding a customer as an insured gives them a direct claim on our policy and complicates renewals.

data.title: SUB-01  Subcontracting and sub-processors
data.contentText: SUB-01 | MSA; DPA | Bramber may use affiliates and vetted sub-processors, with a current list in the DPA and a general authorisation to appoint replacements on 30 days' notice. Bramber remains liable for their performance. The customer may object on reasonable data protection grounds. | Prior written consent for new sub-processors, not unreasonably withheld or delayed, with a deemed approval after 10 Business Days. | Absolute customer consent for each sub-processor, a right to veto the use of cloud infrastructure providers, or a requirement that Bramber's affiliates be treated as third parties. | Elena Marchetti and Tom Whitlock. | Our service runs on third-party infrastructure. A veto right over sub-processors is a veto right over the product roadmap.

data.title: ASG-01  Assignment and change of control
ASG-01  Assignment and change of control
data.contentText: ASG-01 | MSA | Neither party may assign the agreement without the other's written consent, except to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes the obligations in writing. | Customer consent for Bramber's assignment to a competitor of the customer, but not for a change of control of Bramber. | A right for the customer to terminate on any change of control of Bramber, or a prohibition on assignment to an affiliate. | Priya Raghavan. | Investors and acquirers need a clean assignment path. A change-of-control termination right turns a financing event into a customer churn event.

data.title: LAW-01  Governing law and disputes
data.contentText: LAW-01 | MSA; Order Form | English law, with the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales. Before litigation, the parties escalate to senior representatives for 20 Business Days. Either party may seek injunctive relief at any time. | Delaware or New York law for US customers, with courts in those states; German law for German customers where the DPA requires it. Escalation remains mandatory. | The customer's local courts with no escalation, arbitration in a jurisdiction where we have no presence, or a requirement to litigate in more than one forum. | Tom Whitlock; Priya Raghavan for any non-English law. | We are an English company with English insurance and English counsel. A US law clause is manageable; a US court clause with no escalation is an expense we do not need.

data.title: FOR-01  Force majeure
data.contentText: FOR-01 | MSA | A party is excused from performance for events beyond its reasonable control, excluding payment obligations. The affected party must notify promptly and mitigate. Either party may terminate if the event continues for 60 days. | A 90-day termination threshold for infrastructure failures, provided the customer receives a service credit for the affected period. | Force majeure that excuses payment, or an exclusion that captures failures of our own sub-processors. | Tom Whitlock. | Force majeure is for events neither party can control. It is not a cure for a supplier's capacity problem.

data.title: PUB-01  Publicity and references
data.contentText: PUB-01 | MSA | Neither party may use the other's name, logo or trademarks without prior written consent, except that Bramber may include the customer's name in a confidential reference list shared with prospective customers under NDA. | An anonymised case study with agreed facts and a quote approved by the customer; a press release jointly approved. | A blanket prohibition on referring to the customer as a customer, or a right for the customer to approve all future marketing generally. | Aisha Bello and Nadia Iqbal. | References are the cheapest form of proof we have. A blanket ban is usually a procurement default, not a real concern.

data.title: CUS-01  Customer obligations and acceptable use
CUS-01  Customer obligations and acceptable use
data.contentText: CUS-01 | MSA | The customer is responsible for the accuracy and lawfulness of Customer Data, for its users' compliance with the acceptable use policy, and for maintaining its own systems and connectivity. Prohibited uses are listed objectively: unlawful content, malware, unauthorised access, excessive load and use to build a competing product. | A customer-specific acceptable use schedule for regulated customers, provided it does not impose obligations on Bramber beyond the DPA and security schedule. | An obligation for Bramber to monitor Customer Data for unlawful content, or a customer right to suspend fees because of a third party's use of the Service. | Tom Whitlock. | We are a processor, not an insurer of our customers' conduct. The acceptable use policy should be specific enough to enforce and narrow enough to operate.

data.title: UNA-01  Novel and unusual clauses
data.contentText: UNA-01 | MSA; Order Form; SOW; DPA; NDA | Any clause that does not map to a position in this playbook is treated as novel. Examples: AI or model-training rights, benchmarking, ESG or modern slavery audits, source code escrow, most-favoured-customer pricing, regulatory examination rights, and customer-specific service levels. The default answer is no until Legal has written a position. | A time-limited pilot or side letter that isolates the novel obligation, with a documented owner and an exit date. | A novel obligation that is uncapped, perpetual, or impossible to operationalise. Do not accept it simply because the revenue is strategic. | Priya Raghavan. | Novel clauses are where the playbook earns its keep. They are usually drafted for a different business model and import obligations we cannot meet. The correct response is a written position, not a redline in the room.

data.title: INM-01  Indemnities
data.contentText: INM-01 | MSA | Indemnities are mutual, specific and subject to the liability cap. Bramber indemnifies for third-party IP infringement; the customer indemnifies for Customer Data, unlawful use and breach of its own obligations. Each indemnity is subject to prompt notice, sole control of the defence and reasonable cooperation. | A customer indemnity limited to third-party claims arising from Customer Data, with a cap equal to the fees paid in the preceding 12 months. | An uncapped indemnity, an indemnity for the customer's own negligence, or an obligation to defend claims that are outside the scope of the Services. | Tom Whitlock; Priya Raghavan for any uncapped indemnity. | An indemnity is a promise to stand behind a specific risk. If it is not specific, it is a second liability cap with worse words.

data.title: LIA-02  Unlimited liability and carve-outs
data.contentText: LIA-02 | MSA; Order Form | The only uncapped categories are death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, and breach of confidentiality. The IP indemnity is subject to the general cap, with a maximum of 2x the annual fee. | Uncapped liability for breach of confidentiality is acceptable where the customer's data is genuinely sensitive and the DPA contains a matching confidentiality obligation. Do not accept an uncapped data protection category. | Unlimited liability for breach of data protection law, regulatory fines, or “any breach of this Agreement”. These transfer an unquantifiable risk to Bramber and are not insurable on our programme. | Marcus Feld and Priya Raghavan for any change to the carve-outs. | Regulatory fines are not a commercial debt we can price. Our cyber policy responds to incident costs, not to a contractual indemnity for a regulator's penalty. Sample: “Nothing in this Clause limits either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, fraud, or breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality).”

data.title: LIA-01  Liability cap
data.contentText: LIA-01 | MSA; Order Form | Aggregate liability under the agreement is capped at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months immediately before the event giving rise to the claim. The cap applies to each party, not only to Bramber. | 24 months' fees where the customer's contract value is at least £250,000, or where the customer has required a higher cap in a competitive tender. A super-cap for data protection claims of 2x the annual fee is acceptable if the DPA is on our terms. | Uncapped liability, a cap above 2x annual fees, or a cap that applies only to Bramber. These are walk-away positions and require CFO and GC approval. | Tom Whitlock for the standard cap; Marcus Feld and Priya Raghavan for any increase. | The cap is the number the business has priced and insured. Anything above it is an uninsured exposure. Sample: “Each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.”
